docs.title: floci-oci
docs.text:
Light, fluffy, and always free — now for Oracle Cloud

floci-oci is a fast, free, and open-source local Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) emulator built for developers who need reliable OCI services in development and CI without cost, complexity, or vendor lock-in.

It implements real OCI wire protocols so the official OCI SDKs, the OCI CLI, Terraform, and OpenTofu work unchanged against http://localhost:4599.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
docker compose up -d
curl http://localhost:4599/_floci/health
oci os ns get --endpoint http://localhost:4599

See the Quick Start for details.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: Contributions are welcome! floci-oci follows the same architecture and conventions as its siblings floci (AWS), floci-az and floci-gcp.

docs.title: Development setup
docs.text:
Requirements: JDK 25, Docker (for the compat suite).

./mvnw quarkus:dev     # dev mode on port 4599
./mvnw test            # unit + integration tests
make test-java-compat  # oci-java-sdk suite against a running emulator

docs.title: Project structure
docs.text:
io.floci.oci
├── config/           EmulatorConfig (@ConfigMapping prefix floci-oci)
├── core/
│   ├── common/       OciException/mapper, opc-request-id filter, Ocids, OciPage, Etags,
│   │                 ServiceRegistry + self-registering ServiceDescriptor
│   ├── auth/         OCI Signature parsing and opt-in verification
│   ├── storage/      StorageBackend (memory/persistent/hybrid/wal), tenancy isolation
│   └── workrequest/  Shared async-operation plane
├── lifecycle/        Boot/shutdown, init hooks, /health + /_floci/* (alias /_floci-oci/*)
└── services/<svc>/   Controller (JAX-RS) → Service → model/Stored*.java

docs.title: Adding a new OCI service
docs.text:
1. Create services/<svc>/ with <Svc>Controller, <Svc>Service, model/
  2. The service registers its own ServiceDescriptor in an @Observes StartupEvent method, adding a service must never require a service-keyed switch in core
  3. Add <Svc>ServiceConfig { enabled(); } to EmulatorConfig.ServicesConfig + the YAML block
  4. Wire storage through StorageFactory
  5. Add the test trio: <Svc>ServiceTest (unit), <Svc>RestIntegrationTest, <Svc>DisabledRestIntegrationTest (asserts 503)
  6. Validate against the real SDK in compatibility-tests/
  7. Add docs/services/<svc>.md and the mkdocs nav entry

Never invent protocol behavior. Check the wire contract against the OCI SDK sources (the oci-go-sdk generated models are the closest thing OCI has to a machine-readable wire model).

docs.title: Code style
docs.text:
AGENTS.md carries the full list. The rules worth knowing before your first PR:

  • Write explicit types. Do not use var. The concrete type at a call site is usually what a wire-contract reviewer needs to see. The one exception is a record deconstruction pattern.
  • Import the classes you use. No fully-qualified names inline, except for a genuine name collision in that file, with a comment saying what collides.
  • No wildcard imports in src/main. Static wildcards are fine in tests.
  • Never leave a catch block empty. If swallowing is correct, name the variable ignored or expected and say why in a comment.
  • Always use braces in conditionals, and use constructor injection.
  • Tests: JUnit 5 with Hamcrest and RestAssured. Name methods as a camelCase sentence or method_scenario_expectation, never testX.
  • Docs: no em-dashes. Use colons, commas, or periods.

Existing code does not yet satisfy all of these everywhere. Match the rules in code you add or change; leave unrelated cleanups for their own PR.

docs.title: Pull requests
docs.text:
• Conventional commits: feat:, fix:, perf:, docs:, chore:
  • Keep changes focused; behaviour changes come with a test
  • See AGENTS.md for the full operating rules

Please keep no more than 4 open pull requests, drafts included, and no more than 2 of them ready for review. A bot turns a 3rd ready PR back into a draft and closes new ones opened while you already have 4 open. See CONTRIBUTING.md for details.

docs.title: Releases
docs.text:
Stable releases ship on the 15th and the last day of each month. Merging to main does not cut a release: the change rides the next train, and reaches the nightly image on the next nightly build.

Releases are cut from main by the Release Cut workflow, scheduled at 00:30 US Central time on those days (maintainers can also run it by hand). It runs semantic-release over the Conventional Commits since the last tag. That is why the commit type matters: feat: and fix: move the version, docs: and chore: do not. CHANGELOG.md is generated from those messages and is not edited by hand; a genuine correction goes in a PR carrying the changelog-edit label.

docs.title: Emulator Endpoints
docs.text:
Besides the OCI APIs, floci-oci serves a few endpoints of its own on the main port (4599). They are not part of any OCI contract: use them for health probes, init-hook waits, test isolation and TLS setup. Every Floci emulator (AWS, Azure, GCP, OCI) serves the same endpoints under the same /_floci prefix.

They never need a request signature, even with FLOCI_OCI_AUTH_REQUIRE_SIGNATURE=true, and are never refused for a region the tenancy has not subscribed to.

Method Path Response GET /_floci/health 200 with the health body GET /_floci/info 200 with the emulator manifest GET /_floci/init 200 with the init hook state POST /_floci/state/reset 200 {"status": "OK"}, after clearing the state of every service POST /_floci/state/nuke Same as /_floci/state/reset GET /_floci/tls-cert 200 with the TLS certificate (application/x-pem-file), or 404 with a JSON explanation any /_floci/<anything else> 404 {"error": "NotFound", "path": "<path>"}

docs.title: Legacy paths
docs.text:
These stay served, with the same bodies, and are never removed:

  • /_floci-oci/*: every endpoint above, plus /_floci-oci/diagnose and /_floci-oci/config (both {}).
  • /health: the same body as /_floci/health.

The OKE token webhook stays at /_floci-oci/oke/token-webhook/{tenancyId}/{clusterId}, because the kubeconfigs floci-oci generates point to it.

docs.title: Health
docs.text:
{
  "status": "UP",
  "cloud": "oci",
  "services": {"identity": "running", "objectstorage": "running", "queue": "available"},
  "edition": "community",
  "original_edition": "floci-always-free",
  "version": "0.6.0"
}
Field Meaning status Always UP with a 200. Another Floci emulator may answer DOWN with a 503 and a problems map cloud Always oci services Every service, running when enabled and available when disabled version The floci-oci release the image was built from (FLOCI_OCI_VERSION), or dev for a local build

The image's HEALTHCHECK probes /_floci/health.

docs.title: Emulator manifest
docs.text:
GET /_floci/info describes the running emulator, following the Floci Console Contract v2 manifest. A reader must ignore keys it does not know.

{
  "manifest_version": 1,
  "console_contract": 2,
  "cloud": "oci",
  "emulator": "floci-oci",
  "version": "0.6.0",
  "edition": "community",
  "original_edition": "floci-always-free",
  "endpoint": "http://localhost:4599",
  "health_url": "/_floci/health",
  "tls": {"enabled": false},
  "services": {"identity": "enabled", "queue": "disabled"},
  "defaults": {
    "tenancy_id": "ocid1.tenancy.oc1..flocilocaltenancy0000000000000000000000000000000000000000",
    "compartment_id": "ocid1.tenancy.oc1..flocilocaltenancy0000000000000000000000000000000000000000",
    "region": "us-ashburn-1",
    "namespace": "floci-local"
  },
  "ui": {"enabled": false}
}

defaults holds the tenancy used for unsigned requests, its root compartment (the tenancy itself), the default region and the Object Storage namespace. version, edition and original_edition are the keys /_floci-oci/info returned before the manifest; they stay.

docs.title: Init hooks
docs.text:
GET /_floci/init reports the initialization hooks. completed.ready turns true once the ready hooks have run, which makes it the signal to wait on when a test depends on them:

{
  "completed": {"boot": true, "start": true, "ready": true, "shutdown": false},
  "scripts": {"boot": [], "start": [], "ready": [{"script": "/etc/floci-oci/init/ready.d/seed.sh", "state": "successful", "return_code": 0}], "shutdown": []}
}

docs.title: TLS certificate
docs.text:
With FLOCI_OCI_TLS_ENABLED=true, GET /_floci/tls-cert returns the certificate the HTTPS endpoint serves: the generated self-signed certificate, or the certificates in FLOCI_OCI_TLS_CERT_PATH. A private key in that file is never returned. Trust it once and every client validates:

curl -s http://localhost:4599/_floci/tls-cert -o floci-oci.pem

When no certificate is available it answers 404:

{"tlsEnabled": false, "error": "TLS is not enabled", "message": "floci-oci is serving plain HTTP only. ..."}

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text:
All configuration lives under the floci-oci.* prefix; every property maps to an FLOCI_OCI_* environment variable via the standard MicroProfile Config rules (dots and dashes become underscores, uppercase).

Failures are 401 NotAuthenticated. See Request signing FLOCI_OCI_AUTH_TRUSTED_PUBLIC_KEYS – Comma-separated PEM files (public, or unencrypted private) whose key verifies any keyId with that key's fingerprint, whatever tenancy and user it names. docs.title: Resource identity labels
docs.text:
Every container and volume floci-oci creates carries the base labels floci=true, floci_emulator=floci-oci and, when FLOCI_OCI_DOCKER_RESOURCE_NAMESPACE is set, floci_namespace. Function containers that fnserver starts itself are not labelled. A container backing an emulated OCI resource also carries labels tying it back to that resource, additive to the base labels:

Label Value Purpose io.floci oci Cloud provider, for multi-cloud discovery when several Floci emulators share a host io.floci.service e.g. oke The OCI service the container backs io.floci.resource-id e.g. ocid1.cluster.oc1.iad.… The resource OCID, as the OCI CLI and SDKs take it io.floci.compartment the compartment OCID The compartment the resource belongs to io.floci.region e.g. us-ashburn-1 The region the resource belongs to (an OKE cluster's own region). The shared Fn server serves every region and carries no region label floci_service same value as io.floci.service Legacy alias, written alongside io.floci.service; prefer the new key

This makes docker ps --filter label=io.floci.resource-id=<cluster-ocid> resolve an emulated resource to its backing container directly. Applied to Container Engine (OKE) clusters and Functions. The Functions fnserver container is a shared singleton serving every application, so it carries every label except io.floci.resource-id and io.floci.compartment.

The io.floci.* key set is shared with floci-aws, floci-gcp and floci-az, so docker ps --filter label=io.floci lists every resource-backing container on a shared host.

docs.title: Initialization Hooks
docs.text:
floci-oci runs shell scripts from lifecycle-phase directories, mirroring the other Floci emulators.

Phase Directory When boot /etc/floci-oci/init/boot.d Before services initialize — OCI APIs are not available yet start /etc/floci-oci/init/start.d After the HTTP server is listening ready /etc/floci-oci/init/ready.d After start hooks complete shutdown /etc/floci-oci/init/stop.d (or shutdown.d) On graceful shutdown

Scripts run in lexicographic order. A failing start/ready script aborts startup.

# docker-compose.yml
services:
  floci-oci:
    volumes:
      - ./init-scripts:/etc/floci-oci/init/ready.d

#!/bin/sh
# init-scripts/10-create-bucket.sh
oci os bucket create --endpoint http://localhost:4599 \
  --compartment-id "$FLOCI_OCI_DEFAULT_TENANCY_ID" \
  --namespace floci-local --name seeded-bucket

Hook state is inspectable at GET /_floci/init (or the legacy alias GET /_floci-oci/init).

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: Property Default Description floci-oci.init-hooks.shell-executable /bin/sh Interpreter for hook scripts floci-oci.init-hooks.timeout-seconds 30 Per-script timeout floci-oci.init-hooks.shutdown-grace-period-seconds 2 Grace period for shutdown hooks

docs.title: Storage Modes
docs.text:
floci-oci supports four storage modes, selected globally with floci-oci.storage.mode (FLOCI_OCI_STORAGE_MODE) and overridable per service.

Mode Behaviour Use case memory (default) Everything in memory, lost on restart Fast tests, CI persistent Write-through JSON files on every change Durability over speed hybrid In-memory with periodic flush to disk Balanced local development wal Write-ahead log + periodic snapshot compaction Durability with fast writes

Persistent state is written under floci-oci.storage.persistent-path (default ./data, /app/data in the Docker image — mount a volume to keep it).

docs.title: Per-service overrides
docs.text:
floci-oci:
  storage:
    mode: memory
    services:
      objectstorage:
        mode: wal
        flush-interval-ms: 5000

docs.title: Multi-tenancy
docs.text: Every storage key is transparently prefixed with the calling tenancy's OCID, so requests signed with different tenancy OCIDs see fully isolated resources.

docs.title: OCI CLI & SDK Setup
docs.text: floci-oci parses the OCI request signature for tenancy/user context but never verifies the RSA signature — any locally generated API key works. No account, no real credentials.

docs.title: OCI CLI
docs.text:
Create a throwaway key and config once:

mkdir -p ~/.oci
openssl genrsa -out ~/.oci/floci_key.pem 2048

cat > ~/.oci/config <<'EOF'
[FLOCI]
user=ocid1.user.oc1..flocilocaluser0000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000
fingerprint=aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff:00:11:22:33:44:55:66:77:88:99
tenancy=ocid1.tenancy.oc1..flocilocaltenancy0000000000000000000000000000000000000000
region=us-ashburn-1
key_file=~/.oci/floci_key.pem
EOF

Then point the CLI at the emulator:

oci --profile FLOCI os ns get --endpoint http://localhost:4599

docs.title: Java SDK
docs.text:
KeyPair pair = KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("RSA").generateKeyPair();
var auth = SimpleAuthenticationDetailsProvider.builder()
        .tenantId("ocid1.tenancy.oc1..flocilocaltenancy0000000000000000000000000000000000000000")
        .userId("ocid1.user.oc1..anyuser")
        .fingerprint("aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff:00:11:22:33:44:55:66:77:88:99")
        .privateKeySupplier(() -> new ByteArrayInputStream(pemOf(pair)))
        .region(Region.US_ASHBURN_1)
        .build();

ObjectStorageClient client = ObjectStorageClient.builder().build(auth);
client.setEndpoint("http://localhost:4599");

docs.text:

    "user": "ocid1.user.oc1..anyuser",

}

    config, service_endpoint="http://localhost:4599")
print(client.get_namespace().data)

docs.title: Multi-tenancy
docs.text: The tenancy OCID in your signing key's keyId is the storage partition — requests signed with different tenancy OCIDs see isolated resources. Session auth (--auth security_token) signs with a ST$<token> keyId instead; its tenancy is the token's tenant claim, read without verifying the token. Unsigned requests fall back to the configured floci-oci.default-tenancy-id.

docs.title: Regions
docs.text:
Regional resources (buckets, queues, streams, vaults, keys, secrets, functions, clusters) are partitioned by region as well as tenancy. The region comes from the request Host header: the first dot-separated label that is a known OCI region name, so any host that names a region works in it. The simplest way to send one is the public wildcard <service>.<region>.localhost.floci.io, which resolves to 127.0.0.1: for example http://messaging.us-phoenix-1.localhost.floci.io:4599 works in us-phoenix-1. Any other host, such as localhost:4599, reaches the tenancy's home region. Regional OCIDs carry the three letter region key (ocid1.queue.oc1.phx.…), as real Object Storage bucket OCIDs do; some newer OCI services use the full region name there instead.

Identity is global, as on real OCI: compartments, users, groups and policies are shared by every region of the tenancy. Each tenancy has its own home region: a tenancy seen for the first time gets default-region, and keeps it if default-region changes later. As on real OCI, Identity writes are only accepted at the home region (403 NotAllowed elsewhere), and a tenancy can only use a region it is subscribed to (401 NotAuthenticated otherwise): the home region always is, and CreateRegionSubscription adds another at once. See Identity for the details.

Data persisted by an older floci-oci, before region partitioning, is moved into default-region on startup.

docs.title: Wire contract
docs.text:
Every service follows the OCI wire contract:

  • Errors are {"code": "...", "message": "..."} with the correct HTTP status; missing resources report 404 NotAuthorizedOrNotFound exactly as real OCI does.
  • Every response carries an opc-request-id header (echoing yours if provided), and opc-client-request-id is echoed back.
  • Lists paginate via limit/page query parameters and the opc-next-page response header. Identity lists return bare JSON arrays.
  • Mutations carry etag headers and honour if-match / if-none-match.
  • Writes honour opc-retry-token: a repeat of a successful request with the same token, within 24 hours, returns the first response (status, headers and body, with a request id of its own) instead of running the action again, so an SDK retry after a lost response never makes a second resource. A token is scoped to the tenancy, region, method and path. Reusing it with a different request is 409 Conflict (OCI does not document this case for these services; that answer is floci-oci's choice), field order in the body does not count as different, and a request that fails does not use its token up. Object Storage, Functions and Secrets declare no retry token, and their binary uploads are never replayed. Once the resource a token created is deleted (any successful DELETE of its OCID), a retry with that token is 409 InvalidatedRetryToken, as in real OCI. A delete answered with a work request counts once that work request has SUCCEEDED: while it runs, or if it FAILED (a compartment that still holds resources), the token keeps replaying. Deletes that do not go through such a request, like a cascade from a parent or KMS and Vault scheduled deletion, do not invalidate the token, and those retries keep replaying.
  • Async operations return 202 + opc-work-request-id, pollable via the work-request endpoints.

docs.title: Container Registry (OCIR)
docs.text: OCI Container Registry: the Artifacts management API (version 20160918, under /20160918/container) and a Docker Registry V2 data plane, both on port 4599. Images are stored in one shared registry:2 sidecar container.

docs.title: Supported operations
docs.text: Area Operations Repositories CreateContainerRepository, GetContainerRepository, ListContainerRepositories, UpdateContainerRepository, DeleteContainerRepository, ChangeContainerRepositoryCompartment Images ListContainerImages, GetContainerImage, DeleteContainerImage Configuration GetContainerConfiguration, UpdateContainerConfiguration Data plane docker login, docker push, docker pull, and every repository operation of the Registry HTTP API V2 (/v2/<namespace>/<repository>/manifests, blobs, tags)

docs.title: Wire notes
docs.text:
• Every management operation is synchronous. Lists return collection objects: ContainerRepositoryCollection (items, repositoryCount, imageCount, layerCount, layersSizeInBytes, remainingItemsCount) and ContainerImageCollection (items, remainingItemsCount), paginated with opc-next-page.
  • Repository names follow the registry grammar (lowercase letters, digits, ., _, - and / separators) and are unique per tenancy and region; a duplicate is 409 NotAuthorizedOrResourceAlreadyExists. New repositories are private and mutable unless isPublic or isImmutable say otherwise.
  • readme is returned only when it was set.
  • Image counts, layers and sizes are read from the registry, so they always match what was pushed. An image is one manifest digest; its tags are its versions. Image OCIDs are derived from the repository and the digest, so they stay the same across restarts.
  • An image whose tag moved to a newer push stays listed, untagged, as <repository>:unknown@<digest>, until it is deleted.
  • A multi-platform image (an OCI image index or Docker manifest list) is one image. Its layers and layersSizeInBytes are those of its platform manifests, which are not listed on their own and are deleted with it.
  • When the registry cannot be reached or answers with an error, image reads and deletes fail with 503 ExternalServerUnreachable or 503 ExternalServerInvalidResponse, and a repository whose images could not be deleted is kept.
  • RemoveContainerVersion and RestoreContainerImage answer 501 MethodNotImplemented: the registry API cannot remove one tag from a manifest.

docs.title: Pushing and pulling
docs.text:
The registry host is <region-key>.ocir.localhost.floci.io:4599, for example iad.ocir.localhost.floci.io:4599 for us-ashburn-1. localhost.floci.io resolves to 127.0.0.1 and the registry speaks plain HTTP. Docker Engine 29 with the containerd image store uses plain HTTP only for localhost and 127.0.0.1 names, so if a push fails with an HTTPS error, add iad.ocir.localhost.floci.io:4599 to the daemon's insecure-registries. Image references follow OCIR's shape, <host>/<namespace>/<repository>:<tag>, where the namespace is the tenancy's Object Storage namespace (floci-local for the default tenancy).

docker login iad.ocir.localhost.floci.io:4599 -u floci-local/user -p anything
docker tag alpine:3.20 iad.ocir.localhost.floci.io:4599/floci-local/project/app:v1
docker push iad.ocir.localhost.floci.io:4599/floci-local/project/app:v1
  • Any <namespace>/<user> and password is accepted; the token is issued and never checked.
  • A push into a repository that does not exist is refused with NAME_UNKNOWN, unless the tenancy's container configuration has isRepositoryCreatedOnFirstPush: true. Then a private repository is created in the root compartment.
  • An immutable repository refuses manifest pushes with DENIED.
  • A namespace is known to the data plane once its tenancy has used the management API (created a repository or read the container configuration).
  • The data plane only answers on a Host with an ocir label. Hosts of the form <region-key>.ocir.<domain>, <region>.ocir.<domain> and ocir.<region>.oci.<domain> are recognised.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Variable Default Meaning FLOCI_OCI_SERVICES_ARTIFACTS_ENABLED true Enable/disable Container Registry FLOCI_OCI_SERVICES_ARTIFACTS_MOCK false Skip the registry sidecar: repositories and configuration work, image lists are empty, /v2/ answers 503 FLOCI_OCI_SERVICES_ARTIFACTS_REGISTRY_IMAGE registry:2 Docker Distribution image FLOCI_OCI_SERVICES_ARTIFACTS_REGISTRY_BASE_PORT 5200 First host port for the registry sidecar FLOCI_OCI_SERVICES_ARTIFACTS_REGISTRY_MAX_PORT 5299 Last host port for the registry sidecar

The sidecar starts on the first data-plane request, or on the first image read of a repository that has had a push. Its images live in a Docker volume that outlives the container, so they survive a restart of the sidecar or of floci-oci. POST /_floci-oci/state/reset removes the sidecar with its volume.

docs.title: Running pushed images
docs.text:
A function whose image is in this registry runs as it is: create it with the OCIR reference, for example iad.ocir.localhost.floci.io/floci-local/project/app:v1, and floci-oci hands fnserver localhost:<registry port>/iad/floci-local/project/app:v1 instead. The registry publishes its port on the Docker daemon's host, so the daemon pulls from its own localhost, which works for a remote daemon too. The function's image keeps the OCIR reference.

An image is rewritten only when its namespace belongs to a tenancy this emulator knows, so a reference to real OCIR (iad.ocir.io/<real namespace>/...) is passed through unchanged. With FLOCI_OCI_SERVICES_ARTIFACTS_MOCK=true nothing is rewritten.

A pod in an OKE cluster runs an image from this registry by the same OCIR reference: the k3s sidecar gets a registry mirror for its region's OCIR host names. See Container Engine for Kubernetes for how it is wired.

docs.title: Notes and limitations
docs.text: Pull-through cache and multi-region repositories, image signatures, and _catalog are not implemented.

docs.title: Autonomous Database
docs.text:
OCI Autonomous Database (Serverless) on the Database service, API version 20160918 (SDK package database, client DatabaseClient, CLI oci db autonomous-database). Real OCI serves the API on database.{region}.{domain}; floci-oci serves it on port 4599 under the /20160918 root it shares with Identity and Networking.

Management plane only

floci-oci emulates Autonomous Databases in mock mode for now: a database is a record that becomes AVAILABLE at once, with connection strings and a wallet that nothing listens behind. Set FLOCI_OCI_SERVICES_DATABASE_MOCK=true. Without it CreateAutonomousDatabase answers 501 MethodNotImplemented, the only 5xx OCI SDKs do not retry, rather than pretend a database runs. A real database on the Autonomous Database Free container is the next step.

docs.title: Supported operations
docs.text: Area Operations Databases CreateAutonomousDatabase, GetAutonomousDatabase, ListAutonomousDatabases, UpdateAutonomousDatabase, DeleteAutonomousDatabase Runtime StartAutonomousDatabase, StopAutonomousDatabase, RestartAutonomousDatabase Wallet GenerateAutonomousDatabaseWallet Work requests GetWorkRequest on the core work-request client (/20160918/workRequests/{id})

docs.title: Behaviour
docs.text:
• Create takes source NONE (or no source). Clones, backups, refreshable clones and Data Guard sources answer 400 InvalidParameter. compartmentId must be an active compartment, and subnetId and nsgIds, when sent, must exist in Networking. adminPassword is required unless secretId is sent; it must be 12 to 30 characters with an upper-case letter, a lower-case letter and a number, and no double quote or the word admin (Oracle's documented ADMIN rule). It is never stored and never returned.
  • dbName must start with a letter and hold only letters and digits, at most 30, and must be unique in the tenancy (the CLI documents both rules). Names compare case-insensitively, and a terminated database frees its name (inferred). A clash answers 400 InvalidParameter.
  • Echoed fields. Every create and update field that the AutonomousDatabase model also has comes back exactly as sent: dbVersion, characterSet, ncharacterSet, computeModel, computeCount, whitelistedIps, tags and the rest, so Terraform plans no diff. Sizes stay consistent: dataStorageSizeInGBs sets dataStorageSizeInTBs (rounded up) and the reverse.
  • Defaults for what a request leaves out are inferred from Oracle's Serverless documentation, not pinned by the SDK: dbName DB<yyyyMMddHHmmss>, displayName the dbName, characterSet AL32UTF8, ncharacterSet AL16UTF16, computeModel ECPU with computeCount 2, dataStorageSizeInTBs 1, dbWorkload OLTP, dbVersion 19c, licenseModel LICENSE_INCLUDED, isMtlsConnectionRequired true, backupRetentionPeriodInDays 60.
  • Lifecycle. A database is AVAILABLE on create. StopAutonomousDatabase needs it AVAILABLE and leaves it STOPPED; StartAutonomousDatabase needs it STOPPED; RestartAutonomousDatabase needs it AVAILABLE. Any other state answers 409 Conflict (inferred): nothing changes a mock database's state on its own, so the condition never clears and the SDKs should not retry it, as they would IncorrectState.
  • Delete answers 204 with opc-work-request-id and keeps the database readable as TERMINATED, which Terraform and --wait-for-state poll. Every other operation on a terminated database answers 404 NotAuthorizedOrNotFound.
  • Work requests. Every mutation records a SUCCEEDED work request on the core work-request client with one resource of entityType autonomousDatabase (action CREATED, UPDATED or DELETED); Terraform finds the new database's id there after a create. Operation types (CREATE_AUTONOMOUS_DATABASE and so on) are inferred.
  • Connection strings follow the Autonomous Database Free container: the five mTLS aliases <db>_high, _medium, _low, _tp and _tpurgent, TCPS on localhost:1522, service names <db>_<level>.adb.oraclecloud.com. They change with dbName. Nothing listens on them in mock mode.
  • Wallet. GenerateAutonomousDatabaseWallet returns a zip (application/octet-stream, with etag, content-length and last-modified) holding tnsnames.ora, sqlnet.ora, ojdbc.properties and a README. password must be at least 8 characters with a letter and a number or special character. A mock wallet carries no keystore.

docs.title: Wire notes
docs.text:
• ListAutonomousDatabases returns a bare JSON array of AutonomousDatabaseSummary, paged with opc-next-page, and requires compartmentId. It filters on lifecycleState, lifecycleStateNotEqualTo, displayName, dbWorkload, dbVersion, isFreeTier, isDataGuardEnabled, infrastructureType and autonomousContainerDatabaseId, sorts by TIMECREATED (newest first) or DISPLAYNAME (ascending), and lists terminated databases.
  • Create, get, update, start, stop and restart return the AutonomousDatabase body with its etag; the mutations also return opc-work-request-id. Update, delete, start, stop and restart honour if-match (412 NoEtagMatch).

docs.title: Clients
docs.text:
• OCI SDKs and CLI work end to end: oci db autonomous-database create, get, list, update, start, stop, restart, generate-wallet and delete, with work requests read through oci work-requests work-request get.
  • Terraform and OpenTofu cannot apply oci_database_autonomous_database against floci-oci yet. After the create, the provider waits on the opc-work-request-id through its core WorkRequestClient, which it builds outside CLIENT_HOST_OVERRIDES, so the wait goes to the real iaas.<region>.oraclecloud.com instead of floci-oci.

docs.title: Not supported yet
docs.text: Running databases (the Autonomous Database Free sidecar), clones and backups, scaling, ListAutonomousDbVersions, regional wallets, private endpoints, Data Guard, and ChangeAutonomousDatabaseCompartment.

docs.title: Container Instances
docs.text: OCI Container Instances, API version 20210415 (SDK package containerinstances, client ContainerInstanceClient, CLI oci container-instances). Each container instance runs for real on Docker, so its containers serve traffic and write logs you can read back. Real OCI serves the API on compute-containers.{region}.oci.{domain}; floci-oci serves it on port 4599 with the other services.

docs.title: Supported operations
docs.text:
Area Operations Container instances CreateContainerInstance, GetContainerInstance, ListContainerInstances, UpdateContainerInstance, DeleteContainerInstance, ChangeContainerInstanceCompartment Runtime StartContainerInstance, StopContainerInstance, RestartContainerInstance Containers GetContainer, ListContainers, UpdateContainer, RetrieveLogs Catalog ListContainerInstanceShapes Work requests GetWorkRequest, ListWorkRequests, ListWorkRequestErrors, ListWorkRequestLogs

Every instance gets one VNIC on the subnet it names. Networking serves it on GetVnic and UpdateVnic (see Networking), which is what the Terraform provider reads back for oci_container_instances_container_instance.

docs.title: How a container instance runs
docs.text:
• One pod per instance. A pause container (registry.k8s.io/pause:3.10 by default) holds the instance's network namespace on the shared Docker network, and each container joins it (--network container:<pause>), so the containers of one instance reach each other on localhost, as in OCI.
  • The VNIC address is the pod's address. privateIp on the VNIC is the pause container's IP on its Docker network, recorded each time the pod starts, so other containers on that network (the compat suites, a client in docker compose) reach http://<privateIp>:<port>. A stopped and started instance can come back with another address, and the VNIC follows it. A privateIp given on create is kept as sent, and nothing on Docker answers on it. On macOS, the host cannot reach container IPs; use a container on the same network.
  • Images. Each image is pulled before anything starts. An image pushed to the local Container Registry (<region-key>.ocir.localhost.floci.io/<namespace>/<repo>) is pulled from the registry sidecar. imagePullSecrets of type BASIC (base64 username and password) and VAULT (a secret in this emulator's Vault holding {"username": ..., "password": ...}) are used for their registry.
  • Containers. command replaces the image's entrypoint and arguments its command, as the SDK describes them; environmentVariables and workingDirectory pass through. resourceConfig.vcpusLimit and memoryLimitInGBs become Docker CPU and memory limits.
  • Volumes. Each volume of the instance is one named Docker volume, shared by every container that mounts it and removed with the instance: EMPTYDIR on disk, or on tmpfs for backingStore: MEMORY; CONFIGFILE filled with its files before any container starts, so they appear at <mountPath>/<path>/<fileName>. A mount with isReadOnly: true is a read-only mount for every volume type. Volume names are case-sensitive: Cache and cache are two volumes. subPath is stored and returned but not applied.
  • Work requests. Create, delete, start, stop and restart return a work request that finishes when Docker has done the work; the instance is CREATING (or UPDATING, DELETING) until then. A pull or start failure leaves the instance FAILED with the error in lifecycleDetails and on ListWorkRequestErrors; so does a delete that Docker cannot finish (the instance keeps its VNIC and can be deleted again), and a stop or restart Docker rejects fails its work request the same way. A container or volume that is already gone does not count as a failure. Update and change compartment finish at once.
  • Graceful shutdown. Stop, restart, the restart policy and a shutdown of floci-oci give each container gracefulShutdownTimeoutInSeconds to exit before Docker kills it. Left out, it is 0 and the containers are killed at once (inferred: the SDK documents no default).
  • Restart policy. floci-oci checks the containers every five seconds. A container that exited is restarted under ALWAYS, and under ON_FAILURE when its exit code is not zero, and containerRestartAttemptCount counts it; otherwise it becomes INACTIVE with its exitCode and timeTerminated. An instance whose containers have all stopped becomes INACTIVE. The check of an instance runs in turn with that instance's stop, start, restart and delete (each instance has its own queue, so a slow image pull for one never delays another), and restarts a container only while its instance is ACTIVE with nothing pending, so it never undoes a stop.
  • Logs. RetrieveLogs returns the container's stdout and stderr as text (at most 20 MB). isPrevious is accepted and ignored.
  • Restarts of floci-oci. A create that was running is marked FAILED; an ACTIVE instance is started again; a delete that was running finishes.
  • State reset. POST /_floci-oci/state/reset removes the pods and volumes of every tenancy and region. A create or start still running when the reset arrives removes what it started once it finishes.

With FLOCI_OCI_SERVICES_CONTAINERINSTANCES_MOCK=true nothing touches Docker: instances and containers are ACTIVE as soon as they are created, work requests are SUCCEEDED, the VNIC gets the next free address of its subnet, and RetrieveLogs is empty.

docs.title: Wire notes
docs.text:
• Create answers 200 with the ContainerInstance, its etag and opc-work-request-id; every other write answers 202 with only opc-work-request-id. The SDKs record no status codes; these follow the other work-request-driven services.
  • Lists are {"items": [...]} collections with opc-next-page. ListContainerInstances and ListContainers sort by timeCreated (newest first) or displayName.
  • The work request resource has entityType: containerInstance, populated from the start: the Terraform provider reads the CREATED resource from it. WorkRequest has no errors field; errors are on ListWorkRequestErrors.
  • ContainerInstanceSummary carries no containers, vnics or volumes, and ContainerSummary no command, arguments or health checks, as in the SDK models.
  • Deleted instances stay readable with lifecycleState: DELETED.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
• availabilityDomain must be one of the tenancy's (ListAvailabilityDomains), faultDomain one of FAULT-DOMAIN-1 to 3.
  • shape must be offered in the region and shapeConfig within its range (below).
  • There is exactly one VNIC, and its subnetId and nsgIds must exist in Networking (400 RelatedResourceNotAuthorizedOrNotFound). The NSGs must be in the subnet's VCN, and a requested privateIp cannot be one of the subnet's reserved addresses (400 InvalidParameter, see Networking).
  • A volume mount must name one of the instance's volumes.
  • A start of an instance that is not INACTIVE, a stop or restart of one that is not ACTIVE, and a delete of one already DELETING or DELETED are 409 IncorrectState.

docs.title: Shapes
docs.text:
From Oracle's Container Instances Shapes page:

Shape OCPUs Memory Bandwidth CI.Standard.E4.Flex 1 to 64 1 GB (or one per OCPU) to 64 GB per OCPU, at most 1024 GB 1 Gbps per OCPU, at most 40 CI.Standard.E5.Flex 1 to 94 1 GB to 64 GB per OCPU, at most 1504 GB 1 Gbps per OCPU, at most 100 CI.Standard.A1.Flex 1 to 76 1 GB (or one per OCPU) to 64 GB per OCPU, at most 488 GB 1 Gbps per OCPU, at most 40

CI.Standard.E5.Flex is listed only in the regions that page names. The processor descriptions, and the memory an instance gets when shapeConfig.memoryInGBs is left out (16 GB per OCPU, 6 for A1), are not on that page: they follow the Compute shapes of the same series and are inferred.

docs.title: Not emulated
docs.text:
• OCI_FSS_FILE_SYSTEM volumes (400 InvalidParameter).
  • Health checks are stored and returned with status: UNKNOWN; they are not run.
  • securityContext and dnsConfig are stored and returned, and not applied to the containers.
  • subPath on a volume mount is stored and ignored.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
The subnet has to exist first: create one as in the Networking quickstart.

E="--endpoint http://localhost:4599"
TENANCY=ocid1.tenancy.oc1..flocilocaltenancy0000000000000000000000000000000000000000
AD=$(oci iam availability-domain list $E -c "$TENANCY" --query 'data[0].name' --raw-output)

oci container-instances container-instance create $E --compartment-id "$TENANCY" \
  --availability-domain "$AD" --shape CI.Standard.E4.Flex \
  --shape-config '{"ocpus": 1, "memoryInGBs": 4}' \
  --containers '[{"imageUrl": "nginx:1.27"}]' \
  --vnics '[{"subnetId": "<subnetId>"}]' \
  --wait-for-state SUCCEEDED

docs.title: Real-Mode k3s Docker Integration
docs.text:
When real mode is enabled (FLOCI_OCI_SERVICES_OKE_MOCK=false), OKE provisions real local Kubernetes clusters using rancher/k3s:v1.30.1-k3s1 Docker sidecar containers:

  • Control Plane: Each sidecar runs k3s server (Traefik disabled), a self-contained single-node control plane that needs no external server or join token.
  • Dynamic Port Allocation: Each cluster's Kubernetes API server is bound to a dynamic host port in the configured range (default: 6443..6543). The port is published on all host interfaces, so the API is reachable from other machines that can reach the host.
  • Reaching the API from other containers: by default (FLOCI_OCI_SERVICES_OKE_ENDPOINT_MODE=host) endpoints.kubernetes and the kubeconfig server are https://127.0.0.1:<hostPort>, which a client in another container cannot reach. Set FLOCI_OCI_SERVICES_OKE_ENDPOINT_MODE=network when floci-oci runs in a container (as in docker-compose.yml) and the clients are containers on the same Docker network: the address becomes https://<sidecar container name>:6443, for example https://floci-oci-oke-ocid1.cluster.oc1.iad.<unique>:6443. Every sidecar's serving certificate carries its container name as a SAN, so TLS still verifies against the kubeconfig CA. When floci-oci runs on the host, network falls back to host, as floci-aws EKS does. It also falls back, with a warning in the log, when the sidecar's network is Docker's default bridge (or host, none), since those networks have no container-name lookup: run floci-oci on a user-defined network, as docker-compose.yml does, or set FLOCI_OCI_SERVICES_DOCKER_NETWORK to one. The container name contains dots and can have a label that starts with a digit: kubectl and other Go clients accept it, but Java's java.net.URI does not parse it as a host.
  • Lifecycle: CreateCluster returns the cluster CREATING with an IN_PROGRESS work request. floci-oci polls the k3s API in the background; once it answers, the cluster becomes ACTIVE and the work request SUCCEEDED, which is what Terraform and oci ce cluster create --wait-for-state wait on. A sidecar that exits, or an API that is not ready within FLOCI_OCI_SERVICES_OKE_READY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (default 300), marks both FAILED.
  • kubectl Authentication: The kubeconfig is the real OKE token version 2.0.0 shape: its user runs oci ce cluster generate-token --cluster-id <ocid> --region <region>, and its cluster entry carries the k3s CA, so TLS is verified. k3s does not know these tokens, so it sends each one to floci-oci in a Kubernetes TokenReview (a token webhook meant for the k3s sidecar and unauthenticated like every /_floci-oci endpoint, at /_floci-oci/oke/token-webhook/<tenancy>/<cluster>, the same design as floci-aws EKS).
  • What the webhook checks: the token must be the signed https://containerengine.<region>.oraclecloud.com/cluster_request/<cluster-ocid> URL generate-token builds, for this cluster and its region, with an rsa-sha256 Signature over date (request-target) host, a keyId in the cluster's tenancy, and a date within 5 minutes. Like every floci-oci request, the RSA signature itself is verified only when FLOCI_OCI_AUTH_SIGNATURE_VERIFICATION is known-keys or strict (Request signing); by default it is not verified.
  • Who the caller becomes: the Kubernetes username and uid are the caller's user OCID, and the groups are system:masters and system:authenticated, so any accepted caller is cluster-admin. Only a caller whose key belongs to the cluster's own tenancy is accepted, the same rule floci-aws applies to EKS. Real OKE evaluates IAM policy and leaves the rest to Kubernetes RBAC; floci-oci stores policy statements but never evaluates them, so a narrower default would leave every caller unable to do anything.
  • Token lifetime: floci-oci accepts a token whose date is within 5 minutes of now. No Oracle source states OKE's server-side lifetime. generate-token itself tells kubectl to refresh after 4 minutes ("before the token is actually expired", oci-cli containerengine_cli_extended.py), so the 5 minutes is floci-oci's choice, just above that.
  • Prerequisites for kubectl: the oci CLI on PATH with a config whose key can sign (any key works while signature verification is off, the default). Session auth works too: with --auth security_token, generate-token signs with a ST$<token> keyId, and floci-oci reads the caller from the token's tenant and sub claims without verifying it, as the OCI SDKs read them. The same applies to every floci-oci API, not only OKE.
  • Static token alternative: Each cluster also gets a random API token, stored with the cluster and never returned by CreateCluster, GetCluster or ListClusters. Set FLOCI_OCI_SERVICES_OKE_KUBECONFIG_AUTH=token to receive it in the kubeconfig instead of the exec user, for clients without the oci CLI. It is cluster-admin on that cluster.
  • Pulling from the local OCIR: with Artifacts in real mode too (FLOCI_OCI_SERVICES_ARTIFACTS_MOCK=false, the default), a pod can use an image pushed to this emulator's OCIR by its OCIR reference, for example iad.ocir.localhost.floci.io:4599/<namespace>/project/app:v1. k3s runs its own containerd, where that host name resolves to the sidecar itself, so floci-oci writes a k3s registries.yaml (k3s private registry configuration) that mirrors the cluster region's OCIR host names (<key>.ocir.localhost.floci.io, <region>.ocir.localhost.floci.io and ocir.<region>.oci.localhost.floci.io, with and without floci-oci's port, and the same under FLOCI_OCI_HOSTNAME when set) to the registry sidecar over plain HTTP, rewriting <namespace>/<repo> to the <key>/<namespace>/<repo> path the registry stores it under. The sidecar is reached at host.docker.internal:<registry port> when floci-oci runs on the host, and at its IP on the shared network when floci-oci runs in a container. Only the cluster's own region is mirrored. Creating a cluster starts the registry sidecar if it is not running yet; if the registry cannot start, the cluster runs without the mirror. k3s reads the file when it starts, so a cluster created while Artifacts was mocked, or whose registry moved to another port, gets the mirror when floci-oci next recreates its sidecar (on restart, its configuration no longer matching).
  • Storage Persistence: Cluster state is stored in a Docker named volume (/var/lib/rancher/k3s) obeying the global storage persistence and prune-volumes-on-delete policies.
  • Mock Mode: Setting FLOCI_OCI_SERVICES_OKE_MOCK=true (default in test profiles) bypasses Docker execution and returns synthetic control plane state instantly.
  • Teardown: DELETE and application shutdown remove the sidecar container and keep or drop the named volume by the policy above, so a persistent cluster comes back after a restart. POST /_floci-oci/state/reset forgets every cluster and so always removes its volume too, whatever prune-volumes-on-delete says. The anonymous volumes the k3s image declares always go with the container.

docs.title: Wire & Behavior Notes
docs.text:
• Kubeconfig Generation: POST /20180222/clusters/{id}/kubeconfig/content accepts the SDK's CreateClusterKubeconfigContentDetails (tokenVersion, expiration, endpoint). expiration is deprecated in the SDK and ignored. endpoint must be one of LEGACY_KUBERNETES, PUBLIC_ENDPOINT, PRIVATE_ENDPOINT or VCN_HOSTNAME (any case; otherwise 400 InvalidParameter); floci-oci has one reachable API address, https://127.0.0.1:{hostPort}, so every value resolves to it. Which endpoint real OKE picks when endpoint is omitted is not stated in the SDKs or the CLI (both leave it optional with no default), so that case resolves to the same address. Before the cluster is ACTIVE (or in mock mode) there is no CA yet, and the kubeconfig falls back to insecure-skip-tls-verify: true.
  • Cluster settings read back as sent: type, endpointConfig, options, imagePolicyConfig and clusterPodNetworkOptions are stored from CreateClusterDetails and returned by GetCluster and ListClusters exactly as given, reduced to the fields of their SDK types. Nothing is filled in for a setting that was not sent, since the defaults real OKE applies are not documented in the SDKs. Enum values (type, cniType, ipFamilies) are checked (400 InvalidParameter). They are management-plane only: the k3s sidecar does not change with them. availableKubernetesUpgrades is always [] and systemTags {}.
  • Network references: vcnId, endpointConfig.subnetId, endpointConfig.nsgIds and options.serviceLbSubnetIds (and the NSGs of UpdateClusterEndpointConfig and ClusterMigrateToNativeVcn) must exist in Networking; an unknown one is 400 RelatedResourceNotAuthorizedOrNotFound. The endpoint and load balancer subnets must also be in vcnId (the cluster's VCN for ClusterMigrateToNativeVcn); a subnet from another VCN is 400 InvalidParameter. That code is inferred: the SDKs and the CLI do not say what real OKE returns, so floci-oci uses the one Networking answers for the same mismatch. A cluster is not attached to a real network.
  • Cluster updates: UpdateCluster changes the name, version, tags, type, imagePolicyConfig, and the options UpdateClusterOptionsDetails allows (admissionControllerOptions, persistentVolumeConfig, serviceLbConfig, OpenID Connect); the network options set on create stay. UpdateClusterEndpointConfig changes the NSGs, public IP and security attributes and keeps the subnet; ClusterMigrateToNativeVcn gives a cluster created without one its endpointConfig (what Terraform calls when endpoint_config is added later). Both answer 202 with a CLUSTER_UPDATE work request. GetCluster returns an etag, which if-match on these three operations checks.
  • Public endpoint: with endpointConfig.isPublicIpEnabled true, endpoints.publicEndpoint is the cluster's one reachable address, as host:port.
  • Work Requests: Asynchronous mutations (such as cluster and node pool creation or deletion) return 202 Accepted with an opc-work-request-id header, pollable via /20180222/workRequests/{id}. CreateCluster and CreateNodePool return no body, as in the SDK: the new resource's OCID is the work request's resources[0].identifier. A cluster create that fails (the k3s sidecar exits, or is not ready in time) leaves its reason both in the cluster's lifecycleDetails and as an InternalServerError entry of ListWorkRequestErrors, which is where Terraform reads it.
  • Node pools need an ACTIVE cluster: on a CREATING cluster CreateNodePool is 409 IncorrectState (which SDKs retry), and on a FAILED, DELETING or DELETED one it is 409 Conflict. OCI documents neither case, so both are floci-oci's choice. GetNodePool and ListNodePools always carry systemTags {}, as the cluster does, so the oracle/oci provider (9.12 and later) plans no drift after an apply.
  • Immutable Container Naming: Sidecar containers are named using the immutable cluster OCID (floci-oci-oke-ocid1.cluster.oc1.iad.xxx), ensuring display name updates via UpdateCluster do not affect container lifecycle or teardown.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
The VCN has to exist first: create one as in the Networking quickstart.

E="--endpoint http://localhost:4599"
TENANCY=ocid1.tenancy.oc1..flocilocaltenancy0000000000000000000000000000000000000000

# Create a cluster
oci ce cluster create $E --compartment-id "$TENANCY" \
  --name demo-cluster --vcn-id "<vcnId>" --kubernetes-version "v1.30.1"

# List clusters
oci ce cluster list $E --compartment-id "$TENANCY"

# Download kubeconfig (once the cluster is ACTIVE, so it carries the CA)
oci ce cluster create-kubeconfig $E --cluster-id "ocid1.cluster.oc1.iad.demo" --file ./kubeconfig

# kubectl runs `oci ce cluster generate-token` for each request; real mode only
KUBECONFIG=./kubeconfig kubectl get namespaces

# Push an image to the local OCIR, then run it in the cluster by its OCIR reference
NS=$(oci artifacts container configuration get $E --compartment-id "$TENANCY" --query data.namespace --raw-output)
oci artifacts container repository create $E --compartment-id "$TENANCY" --display-name demo/busybox
docker login iad.ocir.localhost.floci.io:4599 -u "$NS/user" -p anything
docker tag busybox:1.36 iad.ocir.localhost.floci.io:4599/$NS/demo/busybox:1
docker push iad.ocir.localhost.floci.io:4599/$NS/demo/busybox:1
KUBECONFIG=./kubeconfig kubectl run hello --restart=Never \
  --image=iad.ocir.localhost.floci.io:4599/$NS/demo/busybox:1 -- echo hello from OCIR

docs.title: DNS
docs.text: OCI DNS is served under /20180115 on port 4599: zones, their records, and private views. Real OCI serves it on the dns.{region}.oci.oraclecloud.com host.

docs.title: Supported operations
docs.text:
Area Operations Zones CreateZone, GetZone, ListZones, UpdateZone, DeleteZone, ChangeZoneCompartment Zone records GetZoneRecords, UpdateZoneRecords, PatchZoneRecords Domain records GetDomainRecords, UpdateDomainRecords, PatchDomainRecords, DeleteDomainRecords RRSets GetRRSet, UpdateRRSet, PatchRRSet, DeleteRRSet Views CreateView, GetView, ListViews, UpdateView, DeleteView, ChangeViewCompartment Resolvers GetResolver, ListResolvers, UpdateResolver, ChangeResolverCompartment, ListResolverEndpoints (always empty)

Not emulated: steering policies and their attachments, TSIG keys, DNSSEC (dnssecState: ENABLED), zone transfers and secondary zones (zoneType: SECONDARY), zone migration, CreateZoneFromZoneFile, and resolver endpoints (CreateResolverEndpoint answers 501). Those that have a route answer 501 MethodNotImplemented; the others have no route.

docs.title: Wire notes
docs.text:
• Zones by name or OCID: every zone path takes zoneNameOrId. A name without scope means the GLOBAL zone of that name. With scope=PRIVATE, a name also needs viewId, or the request is 400 MissingParameter, as the SDK documentation says.
  • Create: answers 201 with the zone, etag and Location. The zone is ACTIVE at once.
  • scope defaults to GLOBAL, zoneType to PRIMARY, resolutionMode to STATIC and dnssecState to DISABLED.
  • A PRIVATE zone needs a viewId (400 MissingParameter) naming an existing view (400 RelatedResourceNotAuthorizedOrNotFound). A GLOBAL zone with a viewId is 400 InvalidParameter.
  • A zone name is unique among GLOBAL zones, and among the zones of one view (409 Conflict).
  • A trailing dot on the name is dropped.
  • Delete: DeleteZone, DeleteView, DeleteRRSet and DeleteDomainRecords answer 204, and remove the resource at once; a later GET is 404.
  • List shapes: ListZones and ListViews return bare arrays. ListZones also sends opc-total-items. Zone summaries leave out nameservers, externalMasters and externalDownstreams, as ZoneSummary does.
  • Records: every record read and write returns {"items": [...]} with opc-total-items, opc-next-page and the zone's etag. Records sort by domain by default (also rtype, ttl). Each record carries domain, rtype, rdata, ttl, isProtected, recordHash and rrsetVersion.
  • Protected apex records: every zone is created with an SOA record and four NS records at its apex, marked isProtected. Adding, removing or replacing them is 400 InvalidParameter. A PUT that lists them unchanged (the OCI CLI's own test sends the whole zone back) is accepted, and a PUT that leaves them out keeps them.
  • Versions: a write that changes the records raises the zone serial by one. version is the serial as a string. Every RRSet that changed, and the SOA, carry the new rrsetVersion; the SOA rdata shows the new serial; the etag changes.
  • PATCH: the operations apply in order to a copy, and the result is stored only if all of them succeed.
  • An operation selects records by any of recordHash, domain, rtype and rdata; ttl is not a selector.
  • REQUIRE with no match, or PROHIBIT with a match, fails the whole request with 412 NoEtagMatch.
  • ADD adds a record, or sets the TTL of one that is already there. ADD with a ttl and no rdata sets the TTL of the whole RRSet, as the SDK documents. The result must still pass the record set rules below.
  • REMOVE removes every match; removing nothing succeeds.
  • On a domain or RRSet path, domain and rtype default to the path's, and a different value is 400 InvalidParameter.
  • PUT replaces every unprotected record in its scope (zone, domain, or RRSet).
  • Record set rules: the records a PUT or PATCH would store are checked as a whole before anything is stored, and a violation is 400 InvalidParameter:
  • a CNAME is the only record at its domain, so there is at most one, with nothing beside it (RFC 1034 section 3.6.2). The apex holds SOA and NS, so it can never hold a CNAME;
  • all records of one RRSet (domain and rtype) share one ttl (RFC 2181 section 5.2). To change the TTL of an RRSet, PUT it whole or ADD a ttl with no rdata.
  • Domains must lie within the zone (400 InvalidParameter).
  • Conditional requests: If-Match on every write is checked against the zone or view etag (412 NoEtagMatch). If-None-Match on GetZone, GetView and the record reads answers 304 when it matches.
  • Views: CreateView answers 201 with an etag, ACTIVE. A view that still holds zones cannot be deleted (409 Conflict).
  • OCIDs use dns-zone, dnsview and dnsresolver, with the region in the OCID.

docs.title: VCN resolvers
docs.text:
Every VCN has a VCN-dedicated resolver. The DNS service creates it, with a protected default view, when Networking creates the VCN, and removes both, with the zones in that view, when the VCN is deleted. GetVcnDnsResolverAssociation in Networking names it.

  • Resolver: isProtected: true, ACTIVE, in the VCN's compartment, with the VCN's display name, attachedVcnId and defaultViewId. There is no CreateResolver or DeleteResolver in the API.
  • UpdateResolver sets displayName, tags, attachedViews (each viewId must be an existing view: 400 RelatedResourceNotAuthorizedOrNotFound) and rules. A rule must be FORWARD with destinationAddresses and sourceEndpointName, as ResolverForwardRuleDetails requires. Terraform's oci_dns_resolver creates and deletes through it.
  • ChangeResolverCompartment moves the resolver and its default view; zones stay where they are.
  • Default view: protected, so it cannot be updated, moved or deleted (400 InvalidParameter). A private zone at or under oraclevcn.com cannot be created in it (400 InvalidParameter), as the SDK documentation says.
  • Attached views: a view a resolver still attaches cannot be deleted (409 Conflict). A default view deleted with its VCN is removed from every other resolver that attached it, and those resolvers get a new etag.
  • Not used for resolution yet: the embedded DNS server answers from every zone, whatever view it is in and whichever resolver attaches it.

docs.title: Resolution from containers
docs.text:
The embedded DNS server answers from the zones of the DNS service, so the sidecar containers floci-oci starts resolve the records managed through the API.

  • Who gets it: the containers started with Floci's resolver: OKE's k3s node, the Functions fnserver, PostgreSQL and MySQL DB systems, and container instances. Their /etc/resolv.conf names the embedded server. A container instance's containers share its pause container's network namespace, and with it that resolver.
  • Only in a container: the server starts only when floci-oci itself runs in Docker (as with docker compose). On the host, the sidecars keep Docker's resolver; set FLOCI_OCI_DNS_HOST_PORT to query the server from the host with dig @127.0.0.1 -p <port>.
  • Which zones: every ACTIVE zone of every tenancy, region and view, GLOBAL and PRIVATE alike. The most specific zone covering a name answers it. When several zones share that name, the oldest answers and the collision is logged at debug level. Views do not scope resolution yet.
  • Answers: A, AAAA, CNAME, NS, SOA and TXT records, authoritative, with each record's TTL.
  • A CNAME is followed through the zones floci-oci holds, up to 8 links, and each link is answered under its own name. A chain that leaves those zones ends at the last CNAME.
  • A name with no records of the asked type is NODATA, and a name the zone does not hold is NXDOMAIN, both with the zone's SOA in the authority section. A CNAME chain that ends at such a name answers the CNAMEs and adds the SOA of the zone it ends in, so the negative-cache TTL holds.
  • Other types (MX, SRV, CAA and the rest) answer NODATA.
  • Names outside every zone are forwarded upstream as before.
  • Changes apply at once: the server reads the zones on every query.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• OKE: k3s's CoreDNS forwards to the node's /etc/resolv.conf, so pods should resolve zone records through the node (inferred from k3s's defaults; not covered by a test).
  • Functions: only fnserver is given the resolver. Function containers are created by fnserver's Docker driver, which never sets DNS servers on them (local/oracle/fn api/agent/drivers/docker/docker.go builds a HostConfig without Dns, and cookie.go sets only the network mode), so functions keep Docker's resolver and do not see zone records.
  • No wildcard records (*.example.com) in resolution, and no zone transfers.
  • UDP only: an answer larger than 512 bytes is truncated (TC), and there is no TCP fallback.

docs.title: RDATA normalization
docs.text:
OCI says "All RDATA is normalized and the returned presentation of your RDATA may differ from its initial input". floci-oci applies the transforms that Terraform's normalizeRData undoes (terraform-provider-oci/internal/service/dns/dns_record_resource.go), so a plan after an apply is empty:

Type Stored and returned as A the IPv4 address; anything else is 400 InvalidParameter AAAA the compressed IPv6 form: 2001:0db8:85a3:0000:0000:8a2e:0370:7334 becomes 2001:db8:85a3::8a2e:370:7334; an IPv4-mapped address stays IPv6, as ::ffff:192.0.2.1 ALIAS, CNAME, DNAME, NS, PTR the name with a trailing dot MX the preference and the exchange with a trailing dot TXT, SPF every word or quoted string as its own quoted string: v=spf1 ~all becomes "v=spf1" "~all"

Other types keep their rdata with whitespace collapsed.

docs.title: Inferred behaviour
docs.text:
These points are not stated by the OCI SDKs, the CLI or the Terraform provider, and follow the closest evidence:

  • Seeded SOA and NS: the Terraform provider skips protected records when it deletes an RRSet, which implies protected records exist; their values are floci-oci's own. The nameservers are ns1 to ns4 under dns.localhost.floci.io, and the SOA is ns1.dns.localhost.floci.io. hostmaster.<zone>. <serial> 3600 600 604800 1800, with TTLs 300 (SOA) and 86400 (NS).
  • Status codes: 201 for CreateZone and CreateView, 204 for the deletes (the SDK documents 204 for DeleteZone), 200 for the compartment moves. No DNS work request API exists, so no opc-work-request-id is sent.
  • 412 code: Oracle's error catalog has one 412 code, NoEtagMatch, which is what a failed REQUIRE or PROHIBIT sends. Terraform only checks the 412 status.
  • Record set rule errors: the SDKs, CLI and Terraform provider state no OCI check or error for a CNAME beside other records, several CNAMEs at one name, or mixed TTLs in one RRSet. floci-oci applies the RFC rules (RFC 1034 section 3.6.2, RFC 2181 section 5.2) and answers 400 InvalidParameter, the catalog's code for an invalid parameter; both the check and the code are inferred.
  • Protected-record errors are 400 InvalidParameter. DeleteDomainRecords at the apex removes only the unprotected records.
  • recordHash is an MD5 of the domain, type, rdata and TTL. zoneVersion is accepted and ignored: no history is kept.
  • GLOBAL zones are regional in floci-oci: they live in the region the request addressed.
  • OCID types dns-zone, dnsview and dnsresolver, all regional.
  • VCN resolvers: the resolver and default view take the VCN's display name; the resolver is isProtected: true; the VCN's deletion removes the zones of its default view; FORWARD rules are stored without checking sourceEndpointName, since no endpoints exist; the association's etag is the VCN's; a VCN's deletion detaches its default view from the other resolvers that attached it.
  • GetRRSet for an RRSet with no records answers 200 with no items.
  • A record PUT without items (an empty body or "items": null) is 400 MissingParameter and changes nothing. items is optional in the SDK models, but Terraform always sends a list, and an empty list [] is how a caller asks to remove the records.
  • IPv4-mapped AAAA rdata is returned in the mixed notation RFC 5952 section 5 recommends (::ffff:192.0.2.1). Terraform compares AAAA through Go's net.ParseIP(...).String(), which prints both forms the same, so either echo gives an empty plan.

docs.title: Events
docs.text: OCI Events, API version 20181201. Rules match the events floci-oci services emit and deliver them to Functions, Streaming and Notifications. Served on port 4599 beside the Functions API, which shares the same version prefix.

docs.title: Supported operations
docs.text: Area Operations Rules CreateRule, GetRule, ListRules, UpdateRule, DeleteRule, ChangeRuleCompartment

docs.title: Wire notes
docs.text:
• Every operation is synchronous. Create, get and update return the rule with an etag; delete returns 204. ListRules returns a bare array of RuleSummary (no actions) with opc-next-page; sortBy is TIME_CREATED, ID or DISPLAY_NAME.
  • A rule is ACTIVE at once, or INACTIVE when isEnabled is false. Each action carries an id, lifecycleState ACTIVE and an empty lifecycleMessage.
  • condition is stored exactly as sent, so Terraform reads back the string it wrote. It must parse as a JSON object (400 InvalidParameter otherwise, null included).
  • UpdateRule with actions replaces the whole list. Every supplied field is validated first, so a rejected update leaves the rule unchanged.
  • An OSS action needs a streamId. A functionId, streamId or topicId that does not exist is 400 RelatedResourceNotAuthorizedOrNotFound while that service is enabled.
  • Rule OCIDs use the eventrule resource type. No local Oracle source shows a real rule OCID, so treat the type as unconfirmed.

docs.title: Matching
docs.text:
Conditions follow Oracle's filter rules:

  • {} matches every event.
  • Every field the condition names must exist in the event with the same nesting, and must match. Fields the condition does not name are ignored.
  • An array matches when any of its values matches.
  • * is a wildcard anywhere in a string value, and a lone * matches any value except null. The period has no special meaning.

A rule receives events from its own compartment and every child compartment.

docs.title: Events emitted
docs.text:
Source Event types When Object Storage buckets com.oraclecloud.objectstorage.createbucket, updatebucket, deletebucket Always Object Storage objects com.oraclecloud.objectstorage.createobject, updateobject, deleteobject Only on buckets with objectEventsEnabled: true

Object events fire on PutObject, CommitMultipartUpload, CopyObject (when the destination is in the same region), RenameObject (a delete for the old name and a create or update for the new one), DeleteObject and BatchDeleteObjects.

The payload is the CloudEvents 0.1 envelope from Oracle's examples:

{
  "cloudEventsVersion": "0.1",
  "eventID": "<uuid>",
  "eventType": "com.oraclecloud.objectstorage.createobject",
  "source": "objectstorage",
  "eventTypeVersion": "2.0",
  "eventTime": "2026-11-18T13:37:11Z",
  "contentType": "application/json",
  "extensions": { "compartmentId": "ocid1.compartment..." },
  "data": {
    "compartmentId": "ocid1.compartment...",
    "compartmentName": "apps",
    "resourceName": "uploads/a.txt",
    "resourceId": "",
    "availabilityDomain": "all",
    "additionalDetails": {
      "eTag": "...", "namespace": "floci-local", "archivalState": null,
      "bucketName": "uploads", "bucketId": "ocid1.bucket..."
    }
  }
}

docs.title: Delivery
docs.text:
Action Delivery FAAS The function is invoked with the envelope as its JSON body (a synthetic result in Functions mock mode) OSS The envelope is put on the stream as one message, base64-encoded in value ONS The envelope is published to the topic as a JSON message (see Notifications)

Delivery runs in the background after the request that caused the event has returned. A failed delivery is logged and never fails that request. An action whose target service (Functions, Streaming or Notifications) is disabled is skipped.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
E="--endpoint http://localhost:4599"
TENANCY=ocid1.tenancy.oc1..flocilocaltenancy0000000000000000000000000000000000000000

oci os bucket create $E --compartment-id "$TENANCY" --name uploads --object-events-enabled true
oci events rule create $E --compartment-id "$TENANCY" --display-name on-upload --is-enabled true \
  --condition '{"eventType":"com.oraclecloud.objectstorage.createobject"}' \
  --actions '{"actions":[{"actionType":"OSS","isEnabled":true,"streamId":"<streamId>"}]}'

docs.title: Notes and limitations
docs.text: Only Object Storage emits events today. Delivery has no retries and no dead-letter handling.

docs.title: Functions
docs.text: OCI Functions, on API versions 20260325 (every current SDK and OCI CLI 3.94) and 20181201 (older SDKs, the fn CLI and fn_go). This is floci-oci's Docker-sidecar reference service: the management plane is emulated in-process, and real invocations run your function image through a shared Fn Project server — the same open-source engine OCI Functions is built on.

docs.title: Supported operations
docs.text: Area Operations Applications Create, Get, List, Update, Delete, ChangeCompartment Functions Create, Get, List, Update, Delete Invocation InvokeFunction (sync, detached, is-dry-run) Work requests (20260325) GetWorkRequest, ListWorkRequests, ListWorkRequestErrors, ListWorkRequestLogs, CancelWorkRequest Catalogs (20260325) ListFunctionsRuntimes, GetFunctionsRuntime, ListFunctionsRuntimeVersions, GetFunctionsRuntimeVersion, ListPbfListings, GetPbfListing, ListPbfListingVersions, GetPbfListingVersion, ListTriggers

docs.title: Two API versions
docs.text:
Both versions serve the same applications and functions, so a function created through one is visible through the other. They differ where the SDKs differ:

20181201 20260325 Create 200, body, etag 200, body, etag, opc-work-request-id Update, Delete, ChangeCompartment 200 with body (204 for delete) 202, no body, opc-work-request-id A function's image top-level image, imageDigest sourceDetails {sourceType: CONTAINER_IMAGE, image, imageDigest}
  • The SDKs declare no status codes; 202 for the operations that answer with only a work request is floci-oci's choice, as in its other services.
  • Every mutation finishes before it returns, so its work request is SUCCEEDED with timeFinished set, which is what Terraform's waiters poll for. Resources are reported as functionsApplication and functionsFunction, which contain the substrings Terraform matches. Errors and logs are always empty, and cancel is 409 Conflict. A change-compartment reports UPDATE_APPLICATION: the SDK has no operation type of its own for it.
  • sourceDetails must be CONTAINER_IMAGE: fnserver runs container images only, so ARCHIVE and PRE_BUILT_FUNCTIONS are 501 MethodNotImplemented. A digest sent with the image is kept; otherwise one is derived.
  • The runtime catalog holds java17.ol9 and python312.ol9, names taken from the OCI CLI's tests; their other values are floci-oci's. No pre-built functions are listed.
  • The optional settings (an application's networkSecurityGroupIds, syslogUrl, traceConfig, logging, imagePolicyConfig, securityAttributes; a function's provisionedConcurrencyConfig, detachedModeTimeoutInSeconds, failureDestination, successDestination, traceConfig) are accepted on both versions and returned as sent. They do not change how a function runs.

docs.title: Wire notes
docs.text:
• On 20181201 there are no work requests: Functions is synchronous with lifecycle-state polling.
  • Lists are bare JSON arrays; ListFunctions requires applicationId.
  • Exact casing matters: memoryInMBs.
  • imageDigest is deterministic per image and changes when the image changes — Terraform's CustomizeDiff depends on this, otherwise plans drift forever.
  • invokeEndpoint is a stable host-only base URL; invocation is raw binary in, binary out — never JSON-wrapped by the emulator.
  • Deleting an application with functions still in it is a 409.

docs.title: Mock mode vs real invocation
docs.text:
floci-oci.services.functions.mock Behaviour false (default) Starts a shared fnproject/fnserver container on first invoke, mirrors the app/function into it, and proxies the call to the real image true No Docker at all; the management plane works fully and invocations return a synthetic body

A new image, imageDigest, memoryInMBs, timeoutInSeconds or config on UpdateFunction reaches fnserver on the next invoke, which updates the mirrored fn in place; a config key removed from the function is removed there too. A new digest for the same tag runs the image pinned to that digest.

The test suite sets mock: true so it never needs Docker.

# Disable the sidecar entirely
FLOCI_OCI_SERVICES_FUNCTIONS_MOCK=true

Real invocation requires the Docker socket — the emulator's container mounts it, and fnserver spawns your function containers as siblings.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
The subnet has to exist first: create one as in the Networking quickstart.

E="--endpoint http://localhost:4599"
TENANCY=ocid1.tenancy.oc1..flocilocaltenancy0000000000000000000000000000000000000000

oci fn application create $E --compartment-id "$TENANCY" \
  --display-name demo-app --subnet-ids '["<subnetId>"]'
oci fn function create $E --application-id <appId> --display-name hello \
  --image <your-fdk-image>:latest --memory-in-mbs 128
oci fn function invoke $E --function-id <fnId> --body '{"name":"floci"}' --file -

To run an image from the local Container Registry, push it there and use its OCIR reference (see Container Registry). The repository must exist first, unless the container configuration creates repositories on first push:

oci artifacts container repository create $E --compartment-id "$TENANCY" --display-name fn/hello
docker tag my-fdk-fn:latest iad.ocir.localhost.floci.io:4599/floci-local/fn/hello:1
docker push iad.ocir.localhost.floci.io:4599/floci-local/fn/hello:1
oci fn function create $E --application-id <appId> --display-name hello \
  --image iad.ocir.localhost.floci.io/floci-local/fn/hello:1 --memory-in-mbs 128

docs.title: Notes & limitations
docs.text:
• Your image must be a current FDK build (http-stream contract). Older fnproject/hello images predate it and fail to initialize.
  • Pre-built functions and archive sources are not runnable (501), provisioned concurrency, trace configs and destinations are recorded only, and detached-invocation results are not tracked.
  • fn-invoke-type: detached returns 202 immediately and runs the function in the background; is-dry-run: true validates without executing.

docs.title: Governance Rules
docs.text: The OCI Governance Rules control plane, API version 20220504. A parent tenancy defines rules for the child tenancies of its organization: quotas, tags or the regions children may use. Inclusion criteria pick the children a rule applies to, and a tenancy attachment records the rule applied to one child. Real OCI serves it on governance-rules.organizations.{region}.oci.{domain}; floci-oci serves it on port 4599 with the other services.

docs.title: Supported operations
docs.text: Area Operations Governance rules CreateGovernanceRule, GetGovernanceRule, ListGovernanceRules, UpdateGovernanceRule, DeleteGovernanceRule, RetryGovernanceRule Inclusion criteria CreateInclusionCriterion, GetInclusionCriterion, ListInclusionCriteria, DeleteInclusionCriterion Tenancy attachments GetTenancyAttachment, ListTenancyAttachments, RetryTenancyAttachment Enforced governance rules GetEnforcedGovernanceRule, ListEnforcedGovernanceRules Work requests GetWorkRequest, ListWorkRequests, CancelWorkRequest, ListWorkRequestErrors, ListWorkRequestLogs (/20220504/workRequests)

docs.title: Wire notes
docs.text:
• CreateGovernanceRule and CreateInclusionCriterion return 200 with the resource, an etag, an opc-work-request-id and a location header. Update, delete and both retries return 202 with an opc-work-request-id and no body. Every work request is already SUCCEEDED.
  • Lists are wrapped ({"items":[…]}) and paged with opc-next-page. Summaries leave out the template. sortBy takes timeCreated or displayName, sortOrder ASC or DESC.
  • ListGovernanceRules and ListTenancyAttachments need compartmentId or governanceRuleId (400 MissingParameter otherwise), as the SDK documents; ListInclusionCriteria needs governanceRuleId.
  • The template is polymorphic on type: ALLOWED_REGIONS needs displayName and regions (known region names), QUOTA needs displayName and statements, TAG needs name. A template whose type differs from the rule's is 400 InvalidParameter.
  • Rules are created in the root compartment (the tenancy OCID) of a tenancy that is not a child. Another compartment is 400 InvalidParameter.
  • CancelWorkRequest on a finished work request, and changing a DELETED rule or inclusion criterion, are 409 Conflict.
  • GetEnforcedGovernanceRule returns an etag that changes whenever the rule is edited or its tenancy attachment changes.

docs.title: Enforcement
docs.text:
ALLOWED_REGIONS is enforced: a child governed by such a rule cannot subscribe to a region outside its list. CreateRegionSubscription answers 400 InvalidParameter and names the rule. A child is governed when it is an ACTIVE member of the organization, its governanceStatus is OPTED_IN (see AddGovernance and RemoveGovernance in Organizations), and an active inclusion criterion of the rule covers it (ALL, or TENANCY naming it).

QUOTA and TAG rules are stored, attached and listed as enforced rules, but have no effect: floci-oci has no quotas or tagging service to apply them to.

docs.title: Emulator choices
docs.text:
The SDKs give the shapes but not the behaviour, so floci-oci picks:

  • Data is global, like Organizations: rules, criteria and attachments are kept with the parent tenancy and seen from every region.
  • Tenancy attachments are kept in step with the rules: a child that becomes governed gets an ACTIVE attachment, and one that stops being governed (it opts out, leaves, or the rule or criterion is deleted) has its attachment set to DELETED.
  • Deleting a rule sets it and its inclusion criteria to DELETED; they can still be read.
  • An enforced governance rule is the child's view of one attachment: its compartmentId is the child tenancy, and only the child can read it.
  • OCIDs: ocid1.governancerule…, ocid1.inclusioncriterion…, ocid1.tenancyattachment…, ocid1.enforcedgovernancerule….
  • The corpus does not say how real OCI enforces ALLOWED_REGIONS or which error it returns; refusing the region subscription with 400 InvalidParameter is floci-oci's choice.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
E="--endpoint http://localhost:4599"
TENANCY=ocid1.tenancy.oc1..flocilocaltenancy0000000000000000000000000000000000000000

oci governance-rules-control-plane governance-rule create-governance-rule-allowed-regions-template $E \
  --compartment-id "$TENANCY" --display-name only-ashburn --type ALLOWED_REGIONS --creation-option TEMPLATE \
  --template-display-name only-ashburn --template-regions '["us-ashburn-1"]'
oci governance-rules-control-plane governance-rule list $E --compartment-id "$TENANCY"

docs.title: Identity (IAM)
docs.text: OCI Identity and Access Management — API version 20160918.

docs.title: Supported operations
docs.text: Resource Operations Compartments Create, Get, List (compartmentIdInSubtree, name, lifecycleState, sortBy, sortOrder, accessLevel), Update, Delete and Move (async, work request), Recover Users Create, Get, List, Update, Delete Groups Create, Get, List, Update, Delete User group memberships AddUserToGroup, Get, List (by user/group), RemoveUserFromGroup Policies Create, Get, List, Update, Delete Availability domains List (3 ADs) Fault domains List (3 per AD) Regions List (every region in the realm of the request's region) Region subscriptions List, Create Tenancies Get Work requests Get, List

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
TENANCY=ocid1.tenancy.oc1..flocilocaltenancy0000000000000000000000000000000000000000

oci iam compartment create --endpoint http://localhost:4599 \
  --compartment-id "$TENANCY" --name dev --description "Development"

oci iam compartment list --endpoint http://localhost:4599 --compartment-id "$TENANCY"

docs.title: Notes & limitations
docs.text:
• The root compartment is the tenancy itself; GET /compartments/{tenancyOcid} returns it.
  • Deleting a compartment is asynchronous, like real OCI: 202 + opc-work-request-id. The compartment must be empty, in every region: no child compartments, no policies, and no resources of any other service (buckets, queues, streams, vaults, keys, secrets, functions applications, OKE clusters and node pools). If anything is left, the work request ends FAILED with a Conflict error listing it, and the compartment stays ACTIVE.
