Otherwise it ends SUCCEEDED and the compartment is DELETED with a random suffix appended to its name (dev.qR5hP2BD), which RecoverCompartment keeps. Deleting a DELETED compartment again succeeds and leaves it unchanged. The work request finishes immediately (real OCI takes a few minutes and passes through DELETING).
  • Compartments nest at most six levels below the tenancy, and a tenancy holds at most 1,000 compartments that are not DELETED, as on real OCI. OCI documents both limits but not their errors, so the codes are emulator choices: creating, moving or recovering a compartment past the depth limit is 400 InvalidParameter, and the count limit is 400 LimitExceeded with a message that starts "Maximum number of compartments", the text the Terraform provider looks for.
  • Availability domains follow the real naming, <prefix>:<region>-AD-<n>: the prefix is Floc for the default tenancy and a stable four letters derived from the OCID for any other, and the region part is PHX and US-ASHBURN for the two original regions and the upper-cased region name elsewhere (Floc:US-ASHBURN-AD-1, Floc:PHX-AD-1, Floc:US-CHICAGO-1-AD-1). Fault domains are FAULT-DOMAIN-1 to FAULT-DOMAIN-3.
  • compartmentIdInSubtree=true is only accepted on the tenancy (root compartment), as on real OCI. accessLevel is validated but not enforced: every compartment is accessible.
  • Region subscriptions complete immediately with status READY. Each tenancy has its own home region, reported by GetTenancy as homeRegionKey: a tenancy seen for the first time gets default-region and keeps it, so changing default-region later does not move an existing tenancy's home.
  • A tenancy can only use the regions it is subscribed to, as on real OCI: a request whose Host names another region returns 401 NotAuthenticated. The home region is always subscribed, and CreateRegionSubscription adds one more at once, so a multi-region setup needs that one call per extra region (by hand or from an init hook). A region outside the tenancy's realm is rejected the same way; OCI documents that rule but not its error code, so the 401 there is an emulator choice. A Host that names no region (localhost) always reaches the tenancy's home region. Emulator endpoints, pre-authenticated requests and CreateRegionSubscription itself are never blocked.
  • Every other service requires its compartmentId to be an ACTIVE compartment created here, or the tenancy itself (the root compartment), as on real OCI: an unknown, deleted or blank one is 400 RelatedResourceNotAuthorizedOrNotFound in a request body and 404 NotAuthorizedOrNotFound in a query. Create the compartment first, or use the tenancy OCID. The check is skipped only when Identity is disabled, since nothing could then create a compartment.
  • As on real OCI, compartments, users, groups, group memberships and policies can only be created, updated or deleted through the home region's endpoint. A write sent with another region in the Host header returns 403 NotAllowed ("This operation must be directed at the home region."). Reads work in every region, and changes are visible everywhere at once (real OCI takes a few minutes to propagate them). Clients that never set a region host reach their tenancy's home region, so they are unaffected. CreateRegionSubscription is accepted in every region: the SDKs do not tie it to the home region, so floci-oci does not either.
  • Policy statements are stored verbatim; the policy language is not parsed or enforced.
  • Customer Secret Keys (/20160918/users/{userId}/customerSecretKeys) are served for the Amazon S3 Compatibility API: create returns the secret once, list returns summaries without it.
  • API signing keys (/20160918/users/{userId}/apiKeys): upload takes an RSA public key in PEM format and returns it ACTIVE, with keyId <tenancy OCID>/<user OCID>/<fingerprint>. The fingerprint is the MD5 of the DER public key, as oci setup computes it. A user holds at most three keys (400 LimitExceeded), list returns a bare array, and delete takes the fingerprint. Deleting a user deletes its keys. An uploaded key verifies requests only when signature verification is on: see Request signing.
  • Identity domains, auth tokens, dynamic groups and tag namespaces are not implemented yet.

docs.title: Request signing
docs.text:
OCI clients sign every request with an Authorization: Signature ... header (draft-cavage HTTP Signatures). floci-oci always parses its keyId for the caller's tenancy and user. Whether it also checks the signature is FLOCI_OCI_AUTH_SIGNATURE_VERIFICATION:

Mode API key (keyId="<tenancy>/<user>/<fingerprint>") Security token (keyId="ST$<jwt>") off (default) parsed only parsed only known-keys an uploaded or trusted key must verify; an unknown key passes unverified must verify against the token's jwk strict the key must be uploaded or trusted, and verify must verify against the token's jwk

A request that fails gets 401 NotAuthenticated with the standard error body and opc-request-id. The message is the catalog's ("The required authentication information was not provided or was incorrect") followed by the reason, such as "the signature does not match the signing key" or "the signing key is not known". It never repeats the signature.

FLOCI_OCI_AUTH_REQUIRE_SIGNATURE keeps its own meaning: it refuses requests with no Signature header. Verification applies to signed requests, so set both to refuse everything that is not signed with a known key. The exempt paths (/health, /_floci/*, /_floci-oci/*, pre-authenticated requests, the OCIR registry protocol and the Notifications subscription links) are never verified.

What is checked, following oci-go-sdk common/http_signer.go, cross-checked against oci-python-sdk signer.py and oci-java-sdk RequestSignerImpl:

  • The signing string is rebuilt from the Signature's headers= list, in the order given, as name: value lines joined by \n. The list is never inferred from the method, because oci-go-sdk's PutObject and oci-python-sdk's enforce_content_headers=False sign a PUT or POST with date (request-target) host only. A listed header that the request lacks fails verification.
  • (request-target) is the lowercase method, a space, and the raw path with ? and the raw query, exactly as the client sent them. host is the Host header.
  • The algorithm must be rsa-sha256. The signature is checked as RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 with SHA-256, then as RSASSA-PSS with SHA-256, since oci-go-sdk writes algorithm="rsa-sha256" for its PSS scheme too.
  • The signed date must be within 5 minutes of the emulator's clock, either way. A signature that does not cover date (or x-date) fails.
  • When x-content-sha256 is signed, it must be the base64 SHA-256 of the body. Unsigned bodies are never read for this. A signed body over 64 MiB is refused.

Which key verifies:

  • An API key: the ACTIVE key uploaded for the keyId's user, in the keyId's tenancy, with the keyId's fingerprint. While Identity is disabled, no uploaded key counts.
  • Any key listed in FLOCI_OCI_AUTH_TRUSTED_PUBLIC_KEYS (comma-separated PEM paths) verifies every keyId with that key's fingerprint, whatever tenancy and user it names. That is how the first CreateUser and UploadApiKey of a strict emulator are signed, the same idea as floci-aws's test credentials, made explicit. A private key file (oci setup keys output, unencrypted) is accepted too, and only its public half is used.
  • A security token: the RSA key in the JWT's jwk claim, which oci-java-sdk's SecurityTokenAdapter reads as the session key. The JWT's own signature is not verified, because Oracle's token issuer key is not available, so anyone can mint a token naming any tenancy. Resource principal tokens, which carry res_tenant instead of tenant, name no caller and are not verified.

Not covered: SigV4 on the Amazon S3 Compatibility API is never verified, because a Customer Secret Key's secret is returned once and not stored. OCIR docker login takes any password, since Identity has no auth tokens.

OKE's generate-token bearer tokens are verified the same way when the mode is not off: the signature over date (request-target) host, with the URL's date, get /cluster_request/<cluster-ocid> and the Container Engine host.

Inferred (no Oracle source states it):

  • Real OCI's exact checks and messages are not public, so the reasons in the message are floci-oci's.
  • x-date in place of date: none of the SDK signers in local/oracle sends it.
  • A Signature with no headers= parameter covers date alone, the draft-cavage default.
  • The 64 MiB cap on a signed body: the SDKs sign only JSON-sized bodies and stream uploads unsigned.
  • Trying both PSS salt lengths (the hash length and the maximum): oci-go-sdk's PSSSaltLengthAuto signs with the maximum.

docs.title: Emulator choices
docs.text:
Behaviour that OCI's SDKs and documentation do not settle, and what floci-oci does:

  • Uploading a key the user already has is 409 Conflict. No Oracle source names the error, so floci-oci uses the catalog's code for a request that conflicts with existing state.
  • Compartment names are unique per parent. The SDK's CreateCompartment comment says a name must be unique across the tenancy, while the compartments documentation says two compartments within the same parent can't share a name. floci-oci follows the documentation.
  • MoveCompartment work requests use operation type MOVE_COMPARTMENT. Identity's WorkRequest enum only lists DELETE_COMPARTMENT and DELETE_TAG_DEFINITION.
  • ListRegions lists the regions of the request's realm, the realm of the region named by the Host header (or the home region), since a tenancy can only use regions in its realm.
  • Changes are immediate. Region subscriptions are READY at once (OCI: IN_PROGRESS for several minutes), IAM changes are visible in every region at once (OCI: a few minutes to propagate from the home region), and compartment delete and move work requests finish at once.
  • Error codes OCI does not document for a rule it does document: 400 InvalidParameter for the compartment depth limit, 400 LimitExceeded for the compartment count limit, 401 NotAuthenticated for a region outside the realm, and a Conflict work-request error for a non-empty compartment.

docs.title: Vault, KMS and Secrets
docs.text:
Three OCI services that work together:

Service API SDK client KMS vaults /20180608/vaults KmsVaultClient KMS keys /20180608/keys KmsManagementClient KMS crypto /20180608/{encrypt,decrypt,…} KmsCryptoClient Secrets (management) /20180608/secrets VaultsClient Secrets (retrieval) /20190301/secretbundles SecretsClient

docs.title: Supported operations
docs.text: Area Operations Vaults Create, Get, List, Update, ScheduleDeletion, CancelDeletion, ChangeCompartment Keys Create, Get, List, Update, Enable, Disable, ScheduleDeletion, CancelDeletion, Import (AES, RSA) Wrapping key GetWrappingKey Key versions Create (rotate), Import, Get, List Crypto Encrypt, Decrypt, GenerateDataEncryptionKey, Sign, Verify Secrets CreateSecret, GetSecret, ListSecrets, UpdateSecret, Schedule/CancelDeletion, versions Bundles GetSecretBundle, GetSecretBundleByName, ListSecretBundleVersions

docs.title: Real cryptography
docs.text:
Crypto is not stubbed. Keys hold real material:

  • AES — AES-GCM encrypt/decrypt. The ciphertext envelope carries the key-version id, so ciphertext produced before a rotation still decrypts afterwards.
  • RSA / ECDSA — real JCA sign/verify (SHA_*_RSA_PKCS1_V1_5, ECDSA_SHA_*).
  • plaintextChecksum (CRC32) is returned on Decrypt and GenerateDataEncryptionKey, as the wire contract requires.

docs.title: Wire notes
docs.text:
• There is no DELETE verb for vaults, keys or secrets — deletion is scheduled via actions/scheduleDeletion and reflected in lifecycleState (PENDING_DELETION), reversible with actions/cancelDeletion.
  • Keys reach ENABLED, not ACTIVE.
  • KeySummary has no keyShape/currentKeyVersion but carries a flat algorithm.
  • The Secret shape never echoes content — content is only readable through a secret bundle.
  • GetSecretBundleByName is a POST with query parameters, no body, and no etag.
  • Single secret versions live at /version/{n} (singular); the list is /versions.

docs.title: Endpoint indirection (deviation)
docs.text:
Real OCI gives each vault its own management/crypto hostname, returned as managementEndpoint / cryptoEndpoint. The OCI SDKs reject endpoints containing a path (endpoint must not contain user info, path, query, or fragment), so the emulator cannot encode the vault in a path suffix and returns its own host for both.

Consequence: CreateKey carries no vaultId, so a new key is attached to the caller's compartment vault — the most recently created ACTIVE one. With the usual one-vault setup this is exact; with several vaults in one compartment, keys land in the newest.

docs.title: Key import
docs.text:
GetWrappingKey returns a real RSA-4096 public key in PEM form. ImportKey unwraps the supplied wrappedImportKey.keyMaterial with its private half and stores the material as the key's first version, with origin EXTERNAL. ImportKeyVersion does the same for an existing key and makes the new version current, as CreateKeyVersion does. Imported keys then work with every crypto operation.

  • RSA_OAEP_SHA256: the material encrypted directly with RSA-OAEP (SHA-256 digest and MGF1).
  • RSA_OAEP_AES_SHA256: a temporary AES key encrypted with RSA-OAEP, followed by the material wrapped with that AES key (AES key wrap with padding, RFC 5649).
Key Lengths (keyShape.length, bytes) Material Wrapping AES 16, 24, 32 the raw key, exactly that many bytes RSA_OAEP_SHA256 or RSA_OAEP_AES_SHA256 RSA 256, 384, 512 the DER PKCS8 private key; the public key is derived from it RSA_OAEP_AES_SHA256 only

As in OCI, ECDSA keys can't be imported: ImportKey and ImportKeyVersion reject them with 400 InvalidParameter.

One wrapping key pair for every vault (deviation). Real OCI keeps a wrapping key per vault and picks the vault from the request hostname. GetWrappingKey carries no vault id and every vault shares the emulator host, so every vault keeps its own wrappingkeyId but they all share one RSA key pair. GetWrappingKey reports the most recently created ACTIVE vault, with that vault's wrappingkeyId as its id. The key pair is generated on first use and kept in the kms storage, so it survives restarts in persistent modes.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
E="--endpoint http://localhost:4599"
TENANCY=ocid1.tenancy.oc1..flocilocaltenancy0000000000000000000000000000000000000000

oci kms management vault create $E --compartment-id "$TENANCY" \
  --display-name demo-vault --vault-type DEFAULT

docs.title: Notes & limitations
docs.text: Key backup/restore, vault replication, external key managers, secret rotation configs and secret rules are not implemented.

docs.title: Logging
docs.text:
OCI Logging covers three APIs, all served on port 4599. Real OCI spreads them over the logging and ingestion.logging hosts.

API Version Use Logging management 20200531 Log groups, logs, saved searches, work requests Logging Ingestion 20200831 PutLogs Logging Search 20190909 SearchLogs with the Logging query language

docs.title: Supported operations
docs.text: Area Operations Log groups CreateLogGroup, GetLogGroup, ListLogGroups, UpdateLogGroup, DeleteLogGroup, ChangeLogGroupCompartment Logs CreateLog, GetLog, ListLogs, UpdateLog, DeleteLog, ChangeLogLogGroup Saved searches CreateLogSavedSearch, GetLogSavedSearch, ListLogSavedSearches, UpdateLogSavedSearch, DeleteLogSavedSearch, ChangeLogSavedSearchCompartment Work requests GetWorkRequest, ListWorkRequests, DeleteWorkRequest, ListWorkRequestErrors, ListWorkRequestLogs Ingestion PutLogs Search SearchLogs

docs.title: Wire notes
docs.text:
• Asynchronous mutations: log group and log create, update, delete and move answer 202 with opc-work-request-id and no body.
  • The work request is already SUCCEEDED, and its single resource names the entity (loggroup or log) and the action (CREATED, UPDATED, DELETED). That is where Terraform reads the new OCID from.
  • DeleteWorkRequest answers 409 Conflict, because there is nothing left to cancel.
  • Saved searches are synchronous and return the saved search with an etag.
  • List shapes: ListLogGroups, ListLogs, ListWorkRequests and the work request errors and logs lists are bare arrays. ListLogSavedSearches is {"items": [...]}. Lists sort by timeCreated (default) or displayName.
  • Names: display names must be unique within their enclosing resource: a log group in its compartment, a log in its log group. A duplicate is 409 Conflict, including one a move to another compartment or log group would create.
  • Delete: a log group that still has logs can't be deleted (409 Conflict). A deleted log group or log then answers 404.
  • Logs:
  • Defaults are isEnabled: true and retentionDuration: 30; the retention takes 30-day steps up to 180.
  • A SERVICE log needs a configuration.source with sourceType: OCISERVICE, service, resource and category.
  • GetLog carries tenancyId, which LogSummary does not.
  • OCIDs use loggroup, log and logsavedsearch.

docs.title: Ingestion
docs.text:
PutLogs takes specversion: "1.0" and logEntryBatches. Each batch has source, type, defaultlogentrytime, an optional subject and entries of data, id and an optional time.

Each entry is stored in Oracle's log format: data, id, source, specversion, subject, time, type, and oracle with compartmentid, ingestedtime, loggroupid, logid and tenantid.

  • JSON data: when data is a JSON object it is stored as an object, so data.<field> queries reach it. Anything else is stored as text.
  • Disabled logs: a disabled log drops what it receives.
  • Retention: entries older than the log's retentionDuration are removed, and searches never return them, even from a log that has stopped receiving entries.

docs.title: Search
docs.text:
SearchLogs takes timeStart, timeEnd, searchQuery and isReturnFieldInfo, and pages with limit, page and opc-next-page.

  • Result shape: each result is {"data": {"datetime": <epoch millis>, "logContent": <entry>}}, the shape the OCI CLI's examples read, until a query projects it.
  • Field info: isReturnFieldInfo adds fields with each leaf field and its type.

The supported subset of the Logging query language:

  • search "compartment[/logGroupNameOrOcid[/logNameOrOcid]]", one or more scopes. The tenancy OCID searches every compartment; any other compartment is searched on its own.
  • where <expr>, where the where keyword is optional. Expressions take:
  • comparisons = != > >= < <=, and, or, not() and arithmetic;
  • string literals in single quotes, with * as a wildcard in =;
  • the functions contains_ci, contains_cs, upper, lower, concat, substr, isnull, isnotnull and rounddown(datetime, '15m').
  • A field such as data.level or type is read from the entry. logContent = '*text*' matches any value in the entry.
  • sort by <expr> [asc|desc], ..., top N by <expr>, dedup <expr>, ..., select <expr> [as name], ... and count.
  • summarize count() | count(x) | sum | avg | min | max | first | last [as name], ... [by <expr> [as name], ...].
  • Comments: -- to the end of the line, and /* ... */, outside quoted values.
  • An unknown function, or a function given the wrong number of arguments, is 400 InvalidParameter when the query is parsed, so a saved search with one is rejected too. A computed value longer than 1,048,576 characters, as a chain of concat() can build, is 400 InvalidParameter.

Unfiltered results come oldest first.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
E="--endpoint http://localhost:4599"
TENANCY=ocid1.tenancy.oc1..flocilocaltenancy0000000000000000000000000000000000000000

oci logging log-group create $E --compartment-id "$TENANCY" --display-name app
# the new OCIDs are in the work requests: oci logging work-request get --work-request-id ...
oci logging log create $E --log-group-id "$GROUP" --display-name api --log-type CUSTOM
oci logging-ingestion put-logs $E --log-id "$LOG" --specversion 1.0 --log-entry-batches \
  "[{\"source\":\"api-1\",\"type\":\"app\",\"defaultlogentrytime\":\"$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.000Z)\",
    \"entries\":[{\"id\":\"1\",\"data\":\"{\\\"level\\\":\\\"ERROR\\\"}\"}]}]"
oci logging-search search-logs $E --time-start 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z --time-end 2030-01-01T00:00:00Z \
  --search-query "search \"$TENANCY\" | where data.level = 'ERROR'"

docs.title: Notes and limitations
docs.text:
These are floci-oci's choices where Oracle's documentation is silent:

  • datetime is epoch milliseconds.
  • JSON data is parsed into an object.
  • Unfiltered results come oldest first.
  • sort and top order missing values first, then numbers by value, then text alphabetically.
  • A compartment scope does not include child compartments.
  • Logs keep at most 100,000 entries.

Not emulated:

  • extend, query parameters ($name, query.from), time_format, and joins across logs.
  • Unified agent configurations and /v2/registry/services (the service log catalog).
  • Archiving to Object Storage.
  • Service logs that floci-oci services write themselves: a SERVICE log records its configuration but receives no entries.

docs.title: Monitoring
docs.text: OCI Monitoring, API version 20180401. Custom metrics go in through PostMetricData and come back out through SummarizeMetricsData with Monitoring Query Language (MQL). Alarms are evaluated once a minute and send alarm messages to a Notifications topic or a stream. Served on port 4599. Real OCI sends PostMetricData to the telemetry-ingestion host and everything else to telemetry; floci-oci answers both on the same port.

docs.title: Supported operations
docs.text: Area Operations Metrics PostMetricData, SummarizeMetricsData, ListMetrics Alarms CreateAlarm, GetAlarm, ListAlarms, UpdateAlarm, DeleteAlarm, ChangeAlarmCompartment, RemoveAlarmSuppression, ListAlarmsStatus, GetAlarmHistory, RetrieveDimensionStates, SummarizeAlarmSuppressionHistory Alarm suppressions CreateAlarmSuppression, GetAlarmSuppression, ListAlarmSuppressions, DeleteAlarmSuppression

docs.title: Wire notes
docs.text:
• ListAlarms, ListAlarmsStatus, ListMetrics and SummarizeMetricsData return bare arrays; ListAlarmSuppressions, GetAlarmHistory, RetrieveDimensionStates and SummarizeAlarmSuppressionHistory return objects. Lists page with limit, page and opc-next-page.
  • compartmentIdInSubtree=true is accepted only when compartmentId is the tenancy (400 InvalidParameter otherwise), as the SDK documents.
  • Alarm and suppression OCIDs use alarm and alarmsuppression. Deleting either leaves a DELETED record that Get still returns and lists hide, which is the state Terraform waits for.

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
PostMetricData validates each metric object on its own and reports rejects in failedMetrics with a message:

  • The namespace starts with a letter and has only letters, digits and underscores. The reserved prefixes oci_ and oracle_ are rejected.
  • The metric name and resourceGroup follow the SDK's character rules.
  • Each metric has 1 to 20 dimensions, with no empty keys or values.
  • Each data point's timestamp is less than two hours in the past and less than 10 minutes in the future.

With batchAtomicity: ATOMIC, one reject rejects the whole batch. Raw data points are kept for 14 days. Older points are dropped once a minute, and a stream left with no points is removed.

SummarizeMetricsData defaults to the last three hours and a 1m resolution. The resolution must not exceed the query interval. An aggregated data point stamped t covers (t - interval, t], and stamps step by the resolution. A query with a condition keeps only the data points that meet it. Streams with no data in the range are left out. An omitted resourceGroup matches only metrics posted without one, as the SDK documents. The time range is capped from the current time by the resolution, as Oracle documents: 7 days below a 5 minute resolution, 30 days below an hour, and 90 days otherwise.

ListMetrics matches name (with * wildcards), namespace, resourceGroup and dimensionFilters. groupBy takes namespace, name and resourceGroup, and ignores dimensionFilters, as the SDK documents.

docs.title: MQL
docs.text:
The supported grammar, from Oracle's MQL reference:

  • Metric[interval]{dimensions}.grouping-function.statistic() condition, for example CpuUtilization[1m]{host =~ "web-*"}.groupBy(host).percentile(0.9) > 85.
  • Intervals 1m to 60m, 1h to 24h, and 1d.
  • Dimension filters with =, != and the fuzzy =~, where * is a wildcard and | separates alternatives.
  • grouping() and groupBy(dim, ...).
  • The statistics mean(), avg(), count(), sum(), min(), max(), first(), last(), rate(), increment(), percentile(p) and absent([period]). The default absence detection period is two hours, and absent(20) means 20 hours. The period must be from 1m to 3d. It counts from when the stream went absent, one interval after its last data point.
  • The conditions >, >=, <, <=, ==, !=, in (a, b) and not in (a, b).
  • Arithmetic with a number on either side, as in 100 - Cpu[1m].mean().
  • && and || between queries, applied left to right. && keeps a data point only where the other query also has one for the same dimensions and timestamp; || keeps the data points of either. An alarm joins its queries minute by minute and then checks that the joined query held for the whole pending duration.
  • Without a grouping function, streams with the same dimensions in different compartments stay separate series.
  • A function given arguments it does not take, such as mean(1), answers 400 InvalidParameter.

Arithmetic between two metrics and nested queries answer 400 InvalidParameter.

docs.title: Alarms
docs.text:
• Defaults: create fills in resolution: 1m, pendingDuration: PT1M, messageFormat: RAW, ruleName: BASE, notificationVersion: 1.X, evaluationSlackDuration: PT3M and the two boolean flags (false).
  • Query: the query, and each override's query, needs a condition or absent().
  • Compartments: metricCompartmentId, like compartmentId, must be an active compartment (400 RelatedResourceNotAuthorizedOrNotFound otherwise). metricCompartmentIdInSubtree: true is accepted only when metricCompartmentId is the tenancy.
  • Durations: pendingDuration must be PT1M to PT1H, repeatNotificationDuration PT1M to P30D, and evaluationSlackDuration PT3M to PT2H. The only accepted resolution is 1m.
  • Destinations: one Notifications topic and one stream at most. A destination that doesn't exist is 400 RelatedResourceNotAuthorizedOrNotFound while its service is enabled.

Every alarm is evaluated once a minute (FLOCI_OCI_SERVICES_MONITORING_ALARM_EVALUATION_INTERVAL_SECONDS):

  • An evaluation at time now reads data up to now - evaluationSlackDuration.
  • A metric stream fires when every one-minute evaluation within pendingDuration meets the condition, or for absent(), finds no data. It is OK again as soon as the latest minute doesn't.
  • Overrides are evaluated in order before the base rule, and the first rule that fires for a stream sets its severity and ruleName.
  • A disabled alarm is not evaluated.

Alarm messages follow Oracle's alarm message format:

  • Fields: dedupekey, title, body, type, severity, timestampEpochMillis, timestamp, alarmMetaData and version.
  • Types: OK_TO_FIRING and FIRING_TO_OK, plus REPEAT while the alarm keeps firing and repeatNotificationDuration is set.
  • Delivery: a topic receives the message as JSON with the notification title, and a stream receives it as one message. PRETTY_JSON indents the JSON.
  • Per stream: with isNotificationsPerMetricDimensionEnabled, each metric stream gets its own messages.

ListAlarmsStatus reports OK, FIRING or SUSPENDED. GetAlarmHistory lists state changes, newest first. RetrieveDimensionStates lists each tracked stream.

docs.title: Suppressions
docs.text:
An alarm is suppressed while one of these is in its window:

  • its suppression window;
  • an ACTIVE alarm suppression of level ALARM that targets the alarm, its compartment, or the tenancy with compartmentIdInSubtree.

A suppressed alarm is not evaluated and reports SUSPENDED. A DIMENSION suppression, the default level, which needs dimensions, silences only the streams whose dimensions include the suppressed ones.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
E="--endpoint http://localhost:4599"
TENANCY=ocid1.tenancy.oc1..flocilocaltenancy0000000000000000000000000000000000000000
NOW=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)

oci monitoring metric-data post $E --metric-data "[{\"namespace\":\"my_app\",\"compartmentId\":\"$TENANCY\",
  \"name\":\"latency\",\"dimensions\":{\"host\":\"web-1\"},\"datapoints\":[{\"timestamp\":\"$NOW\",\"value\":120}]}]"
oci monitoring metric-data summarize-metrics-data $E --compartment-id "$TENANCY" \
  --namespace my_app --query-text 'latency[1m].max()'

docs.title: Notes and limitations
docs.text:
These are floci-oci's choices where Oracle's documentation is silent:

  • The aggregation window (t - interval, t].
  • rate() and increment() are worked out inside one window.
  • The system-generated alarmSummary text.
  • The 14 day retention.
  • Where the absence detection period starts: one interval after the stream's last data point.
  • A dimension name in a filter is any name ingestion accepts (printable ASCII without spaces), ended by =, !, ~, ,, {, } or ", so a name containing one of those cannot be filtered.

Not emulated:

  • RESET messages and the internal reset period.
  • Dynamic variables in body and notificationTitle, which are sent as written.
  • The ONS_OPTIMIZED layout, which is sent as RAW.
  • Evaluation of recurrence suppressionConditions: a suppression with conditions applies across its whole window.
  • The serviceName and entityId filters of ListAlarmsStatus.
  • Service metrics: only custom metrics exist.
  • Gzip-encoded PostMetricData bodies.

docs.title: MySQL HeatWave
docs.text: OCI MySQL HeatWave DB systems, API version 20190415 (SDK package mysql, clients DbSystemClient, MysqlaasClient and WorkRequestsClient, CLI oci mysql). Each DB system is backed by a real MySQL container, so the endpoint GetDbSystem returns is one an application can connect to with the admin user it was created with. Real OCI serves the API on mysql.{region}.ocp.{domain}; floci-oci serves it on port 4599 with the other services.

docs.title: Supported operations
docs.text: Area Operations DB systems CreateDbSystem, GetDbSystem, ListDbSystems, UpdateDbSystem, DeleteDbSystem Runtime StartDbSystem, StopDbSystem, RestartDbSystem Catalog ListShapes, ListVersions Configurations CreateConfiguration, GetConfiguration, ListConfigurations, UpdateConfiguration, DeleteConfiguration Work requests GetWorkRequest, ListWorkRequests, ListWorkRequestErrors, ListWorkRequestLogs, CancelWorkRequest

docs.title: How a DB system runs
docs.text:
• One container per DB system. CreateDbSystem returns the system CREATING with an IN_PROGRESS work request and starts a mysql:<version> container in the background. Once MySQL answers on TCP the system becomes ACTIVE and the work request SUCCEEDED. Terraform waits on the lifecycle state, oci mysql db-system create --wait-for-state on the work request. A container that exits, or one that is not ready within FLOCI_OCI_SERVICES_MYSQL_READY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (default 180), marks the system FAILED (MySQL has no NEEDS_ATTENTION state) and its work request FAILED, with the reason listed by ListWorkRequestErrors.
  • Version and image. mysqlVersion takes a version from ListVersions (8.4.4) or a family (8.4, its newest version); without one a DB system runs 8.4.4. The version picks the image through FLOCI_OCI_SERVICES_MYSQL_IMAGE (default mysql:{version}). A new mysqlVersion on UpdateDbSystem restarts the server on the new image.
  • Admin user. adminUsername and adminPassword are required when the sidecar runs. The admin is created with every privilege on the first start; the password is not stored. A new adminPassword on UpdateDbSystem is accepted and not applied to the server.
  • Endpoint. MySQL's port is published on a host port from FLOCI_OCI_SERVICES_MYSQL_BASE_PORT..MAX_PORT (default 13306..13405), one per DB system, and endpoints[0] carries the host and port to connect to: localhost and that port when floci-oci runs on the host, the container's name and 3306 when it runs in a container (clients on the same Docker network). The top-level port and portX stay as requested (default 3306 and 33060), since Terraform replaces a DB system whose port changes. The X Protocol port is not published.
  • Stop, start and restart keep the data volume. StopDbSystem and RestartDbSystem require shutdownType (IMMEDIATE, FAST or SLOW); the container is stopped the same way for each.
  • Delete removes the container. The data volume goes with it in memory storage mode or when FLOCI_OCI_STORAGE_PRUNE_VOLUMES_ON_DELETE is set. The system stays readable as DELETED.
  • Mock mode (FLOCI_OCI_SERVICES_MYSQL_MOCK=true) starts nothing: DB systems become ACTIVE at once, with an endpoint nothing listens on, and the admin credentials are optional.

docs.title: Wire notes
docs.text:
• Every list returns a bare JSON array ([]DbSystemSummary, []ShapeSummary, []VersionSummary, []ConfigurationSummary, []WorkRequestSummary), paged with opc-next-page where the SDK pages it; ListShapes and ListVersions are not paged. Every list requires compartmentId.
  • CreateDbSystem answers 200 with the DbSystem, etag, location and opc-work-request-id. Update, delete, start, stop and restart answer 202 with only opc-work-request-id. The SDKs record no status codes; these follow the other floci-oci services with work requests.
  • adminUsername and adminPassword never appear in a response, as in the SDK model.
  • source is always {"sourceType": "NONE"}.
  • subnetId and nsgIds must exist in Networking, otherwise 400 RelatedResourceNotAuthorizedOrNotFound. Nothing is attached to a real network.

docs.title: Emulator choices
docs.text:
These defaults are floci-oci's own; no Oracle source in the reference corpus states them.

  • When omitted: dataStorageSizeInGBs 50, fault domain FAULT-DOMAIN-1, maintenance window SUN 00:00, a backup policy enabled with window 00:00 and 7 days of retention, deletionPolicy DELETE / SKIP_FINAL_BACKUP / not protected, crashRecovery ENABLED, databaseManagement DISABLED, READ_WRITE / UNRESTRICTED, and system-generated certificates. A display name defaults to mysqldbsystem<timestamp>.
  • The maintenance window comes back exactly as sent (sun 01:00 stays lowercase), since Terraform compares it as a string.
  • A DB system with deletionPolicy.isDeleteProtected true answers DeleteDbSystem with 409 Conflict until the protection is turned off.
  • A FAILED DB system still takes an UpdateDbSystem that changes only deletionPolicy, displayName, description or tags, so a protected system whose container never started can be unprotected and deleted. Any other field answers 409 Conflict. OCI does not document updates in FAILED; this rule is inferred.
  • CancelWorkRequest answers 409 Conflict: operations are not cancellable.
  • An operation the DB system's state does not allow is refused with 409. A refusal while the system is CREATING, UPDATING or DELETING is 409 IncorrectState, which OCI SDKs retry until the operation finishes; in any other state a retry cannot succeed, so it is 409 Conflict, which they do not retry.
  • dataStorageSizeInGBs may grow, never shrink (400 InvalidParameter). Storage limits, backup policies and maintenance windows are recorded, not acted on.

docs.title: Shapes, versions and configurations
docs.text:
• Shapes and their CPU and memory sizes come from Oracle's Supported Shapes page: the ECPU shapes (MySQL.Free, MySQL.2 to MySQL.384), a subset of the OCPU shapes (MySQL.VM.Standard.E3.*, E4.*, Standard3.*) and the MySQL.HeatWave.* shapes. isSupportedFor lists HEATWAVECLUSTER for the shapes that page says support one. A shape changes nothing about the container.
  • Versions are a subset of Oracle's MySQL Server Versions, picked so each one exists as a mysql image tag: 8.0.39 to 8.0.41, 8.4.2 to 8.4.4, 9.1.0 and 9.2.0. The family labels (8.4 - Long Term Support release) are floci-oci's.
  • Default configurations are <shape>.Standalone and <shape>.HA for every shape, the names Oracle's page gives. Their OCIDs are stable across restarts, they belong to the tenancy, and they carry no variables. A DB system created without configurationId gets the Standalone (or, with isHighlyAvailable, the HA) default of its shape.
  • Custom configurations take a shapeName, an optional parentConfigurationId whose variables they start from, and variables. The variables are stored and returned but not applied to the server. A configuration a DB system uses cannot be deleted (409 Conflict), and a DB system's configuration must be for its shape (400 InvalidParameter).

docs.title: Not emulated
docs.text: Backups and restore, HeatWave clusters, read replicas, channels, blue-green deployments, maintenance events and DB system status reports. Creating a DB system from a source other than NONE answers 400 InvalidParameter. isHighlyAvailable is recorded; there is one server either way.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
The subnet has to exist first: create one as in the Networking quickstart.

E="--endpoint http://localhost:4599"
TENANCY=ocid1.tenancy.oc1..flocilocaltenancy0000000000000000000000000000000000000000

# Create a DB system and wait for it
oci mysql db-system create $E --compartment-id "$TENANCY" --shape-name MySQL.2 \
  --subnet-id <subnetId> --admin-username admin_user --admin-password 'BEstrO0ng_#11' \
  --wait-for-state SUCCEEDED

# Where to connect
oci mysql db-system get $E --db-system-id <dbSystemId> --query 'data.endpoints[0]'
mysql -h 127.0.0.1 -P <port> -u admin_user -p

docs.title: Networking (VCN)
docs.text: OCI Core Virtual Network, API version 20160918. Real OCI serves it on the iaas.<region> host under the same version prefix as Identity; floci-oci serves both on port 4599. Resources are kept as state only: no Docker network is created for a VCN.

docs.title: Supported operations
docs.text: Area Operations VCNs CreateVcn, GetVcn, ListVcns, UpdateVcn, DeleteVcn, ChangeVcnCompartment, GetVcnDnsResolverAssociation Subnets CreateSubnet, GetSubnet, ListSubnets, UpdateSubnet, DeleteSubnet, ChangeSubnetCompartment Gateways Internet, NAT and service gateways: Create, Get, List, Update, Delete, ChangeCompartment; AttachServiceId, DetachServiceId Services ListServices, GetService Route tables Create, Get, List, Update, Delete, ChangeCompartment Security lists Create, Get, List, Update, Delete, ChangeCompartment Network security groups Create, Get, List, Update, Delete, ChangeCompartment; AddNetworkSecurityGroupSecurityRules, UpdateNetworkSecurityGroupSecurityRules, RemoveNetworkSecurityGroupSecurityRules, ListNetworkSecurityGroupSecurityRules, ListNetworkSecurityGroupVnics VNICs GetVnic, UpdateVnic (VNICs are created by the services that attach them) DHCP options Create, Get, List, Update, Delete, ChangeCompartment

docs.title: Wire notes
docs.text:
• Create, get and update return the resource with an etag header (CreateServiceGateway returns none); delete returns 204. Lists are bare JSON arrays paginated with opc-next-page. sortBy=TIMECREATED sorts newest first, DISPLAYNAME A to Z.
  • Every resource is AVAILABLE as soon as it is created. A deleted resource reads as 404 NotAuthorizedOrNotFound, which Terraform accepts as gone.
  • CreateVcn makes three defaults and returns their OCIDs as defaultRouteTableId, defaultSecurityListId and defaultDhcpOptionsId: Default Route Table for <name> (no rules), Default Security List for <name> (ingress TCP 22 and ICMP 3/4 from anywhere, ICMP 3 from the VCN, all egress) and Default DHCP Options for <name> (VcnLocalPlusInternet, plus a <dnsLabel>.oraclevcn.com search domain when the VCN has a DNS label). Defaults cannot be deleted on their own; they go with the VCN.
  • A subnet without routeTableId, securityListIds or dhcpOptionsId uses the VCN's defaults. virtualRouterIp is the first host address of the subnet.
  • Route rules come back with both cidrBlock and destination, destinationType (CIDR_BLOCK by default) and routeType: STATIC, as Terraform expects.
  • ListServices returns All <CODE> Services In Oracle Services Network and OCI <CODE> Object Storage for the region; their OCIDs are stable across restarts.
  • VCN and subnet compartment moves return 202 with opc-work-request-id, polled at /20160918/workRequests/{id} (the path the Core work-request client uses). The other compartment moves return 200.

docs.title: DNS resolver association
docs.text: Every VCN gets a VCN-dedicated DNS resolver with a protected default view, created by the DNS service when the VCN is created and removed when it is deleted. GET /20160918/vcns/{vcnId}/dnsResolverAssociation answers vcnId, dnsResolverId and lifecycleState: AVAILABLE, with the VCN's etag. A VCN created while DNS was disabled gets its resolver the first time the association is read; with DNS disabled the association has no dnsResolverId.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
Request Result VCN CIDR outside /16 to /30, or overlapping CIDR blocks 400 InvalidParameter Subnet CIDR outside the VCN, or overlapping another subnet 400 InvalidParameter dnsLabel not a letter followed by letters and digits (15 max), or reused in the VCN 400 InvalidParameter Route rule with different cidrBlock and destination 400 InvalidParameter Unknown vcnId, route table, security list, DHCP options, gateway or service in a body 400 RelatedResourceNotAuthorizedOrNotFound Delete a VCN that still has subnets, gateways or non-default resources 409 Conflict Delete a route table, security list or DHCP options a subnet uses, or a gateway a route rule targets 409 Conflict Delete a VCN, subnet or network security group another service's resource still uses (an OKE cluster, a function application, a PostgreSQL or MySQL DB system, an Autonomous Database, a container instance's VNIC) 409 Conflict

A resource that another service holds a reference to stays until that resource is deleted: the 409 Conflict names each one (application ocid1.fnapp...). A deleted resource no longer counts, but one that is still DELETING does, as in OCI, where the Terraform provider retries a subnet delete on Conflict while its dependants are torn down. The status and code follow OCI; the message wording is floci-oci's own (inferred, no source shows OCI's text). A resource that is still being created or updated with the VCN, subnet or NSG counts too, from the moment its references are checked until it is saved (an OKE cluster starts its k3s sidecar in between), so a delete in that window is refused rather than leaving it pointing at a deleted network.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
E="--endpoint http://localhost:4599"
TENANCY=ocid1.tenancy.oc1..flocilocaltenancy0000000000000000000000000000000000000000

VCN=$(oci network vcn create $E --compartment-id "$TENANCY" --cidr-blocks '["10.0.0.0/16"]' \
  --dns-label main --query data.id --raw-output)
oci network subnet create $E --compartment-id "$TENANCY" --vcn-id "$VCN" \
  --cidr-block 10.0.1.0/24 --dns-label app
oci network internet-gateway create $E --compartment-id "$TENANCY" --vcn-id "$VCN" --is-enabled true

With Terraform, add oci_core.VirtualNetworkClient to client_host_overrides in the provider block.

docs.title: VNICs
docs.text: A VNIC is created by the service that places something on a subnet, today Container Instances, and deleted with it; there is no CreateVnic. GetVnic returns the Vnic shape of oci-go-sdk/core/vnic.go: subnetId, availabilityDomain, privateIp, hostnameLabel, nsgIds, skipSourceDestCheck, isPrimary: true, a synthetic macAddress, and publicIp only when one was asked for. The private IP is the one requested, the address the workload really got (a container instance in real mode), or else the next free one in the subnet, skipping the first two and the last address, which OCI keeps for the network, the virtual router and the broadcast. A requested address outside the subnet, or one of those three reserved addresses, is 400 InvalidParameter, one already in use 409 Conflict. Oracle's VCN overview documents the reservation; the error code for requesting a reserved address is inferred. A workload address changes with the workload (a restarted pod can get another); a requested or allocated one never does. A public IP, when asked for, comes from 203.0.113.0/24 (documentation addresses, RFC 5737): nothing floci-oci hands out is publicly routable. UpdateVnic changes the display name, hostname label, NSGs, skipSourceDestCheck and tags, and checks if-match. On attach and on update every NSG must be in the subnet's VCN, or the request is 400 InvalidParameter (nsgIds <id> belongs to another VCN, the rule subnets already apply to route tables and security lists; inferred, as no source states the error). ListNetworkSecurityGroupVnics lists the VNICs in a group. A subnet with VNICs cannot be deleted (409 Conflict).

docs.title: Notes and limitations
docs.text:
VCN and subnet CIDR changes (add, modify and remove CIDR, IPv6), VLANs, DRGs, local peering gateways, and private and public IP objects are not implemented.

OKE, Functions and Database with PostgreSQL check every VCN, subnet and network security group OCID they receive against this service: one that does not exist in the caller's tenancy and region is rejected with 400 RelatedResourceNotAuthorizedOrNotFound. With Networking disabled (FLOCI_OCI_SERVICES_NETWORKING_ENABLED=false) they accept any OCID.

docs.title: NoSQL Database
docs.text: OCI NoSQL Database Cloud Service, API version 20190828. Tables are created from DDL statements, rows are written and read one at a time by primary key, and a SELECT subset of the NoSQL SQL dialect queries them. Everything runs in process on port 4599.

docs.title: Supported operations
docs.text:
Area Operations Tables CreateTable, GetTable, ListTables, UpdateTable, DeleteTable, ChangeTableCompartment, ListTableUsage Indexes CreateIndex, GetIndex, ListIndexes, DeleteIndex Rows UpdateRow (put), GetRow, DeleteRow Query Query, PrepareStatement, SummarizeStatement Work requests GetWorkRequest, ListWorkRequests, ListWorkRequestErrors, ListWorkRequestLogs, DeleteWorkRequest

Not served: replicas (/tables/{t}/replicas), /configuration and its KMS key actions, and the native driver protocol (/V2/nosql/data) that the Java, Python, Go and Node NoSQL drivers speak. Only the OCI REST API is emulated, so use the OCI SDKs, the OCI CLI or Terraform.

docs.title: Wire notes
docs.text:
• Table and index mutations are work-request driven: 202, an opc-work-request-id header and no body. The work request is already SUCCEEDED with timeFinished set, and its one resource is entityType: TABLE, actionType CREATED, UPDATED or DELETED, and identifier the table OCID. Terraform's oci_nosql_table and oci_nosql_index wait on exactly that resource.
  • The work request operationType enum has only CREATE_TABLE, UPDATE_TABLE, DELETE_TABLE and UPDATE_CONFIGURATION, so CreateIndex, DeleteIndex and ChangeTableCompartment all report UPDATE_TABLE.
  • {tableNameOrId} is the table OCID, or the table name together with compartmentId. A name without compartmentId is 400 MissingParameter. Table names match case-insensitively.
  • ddlStatement is echoed verbatim: GetTable returns the last DDL statement the table received, the CREATE TABLE or the latest ALTER TABLE. Terraform reads it back and compares it, ignoring case only.
  • A deleted table stays readable by OCID as a DELETED tombstone. A name lookup, a write or a query no longer finds it, and the name can be reused. ListTables omits DELETED tables unless lifecycleState=DELETED or ALL asks for them.
  • Lists are wrapped ({"items":[…]}) and paginate with limit, page and opc-next-page. TableCollection also carries autoReclaimableTables, onDemandCapacityTables and an empty availableReplicationRegions.
  • Condition failures are results, not errors. An UpdateRow whose option (IF_ABSENT, IF_PRESENT) or if-match version does not hold is a 200 without version; with isGetReturnRow it carries existingVersion and existingValue. A DeleteRow that finds no row, or whose if-match does not match, is a 200 with isSuccess: false.
  • GetRow and DeleteRow take key as a repeated query parameter, one column:value per primary key column: ?key=tenant:acme&key=id:1.
  • etag on UpdateRow and GetRow is the row version.
  • Query takes limit/page and returns {"items":[…], "usage":{…}} with opc-next-page; without limit a page holds 100 results.

docs.title: DDL subset
docs.text:
CREATE TABLE [IF NOT EXISTS] name (
    column type [GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY | GENERATED BY DEFAULT [ON NULL] AS IDENTITY [(START WITH n INCREMENT BY m)]]
                [NOT NULL] [DEFAULT literal] [COMMENT "text"],
    ...,
    PRIMARY KEY ([SHARD(column, ...),] column, ...)
) [USING TTL n DAYS|HOURS]

ALTER TABLE name (ADD column type ..., DROP column, ...)
ALTER TABLE name USING TTL n DAYS|HOURS
CREATE INDEX [IF NOT EXISTS] name ON table (column[.json.path] [AS type], ...)
DROP TABLE [IF EXISTS] name
DROP INDEX [IF EXISTS] name ON table

Types: INTEGER, LONG, FLOAT, DOUBLE, NUMBER, STRING (with AS UUID [GENERATED BY DEFAULT]), BOOLEAN, BINARY[(n)], TIMESTAMP[(p)], ENUM(...), ARRAY(type), MAP(type), RECORD(field type, ...) and JSON. Without SHARD(...) the shard key is the whole primary key. As Oracle's reference says, a trailing semicolon is an error, and a NOT NULL column needs a DEFAULT. CreateTable takes only CREATE TABLE and UpdateTable only ALTER TABLE. CREATE INDEX and the DROP statements are understood by SummarizeStatement; use the CreateIndex, DeleteIndex and DeleteTable operations to run them. A DDL syntax error is 400 InvalidParameter, and SummarizeStatement reports it as syntaxError.

docs.title: Rows
docs.text:
• UpdateRow checks each value against its column type and fills GENERATED identity and UUID columns; generatedValue returns the generated value. Giving a value for a GENERATED ALWAYS identity column is 400 InvalidParameter.
  • Fields that are not columns are ignored, and missing columns take their DEFAULT or null, unless isExactMatch is true, which makes either a 400.
  • ttl (days) sets the row's expiry; 0 means never. Without it, a new row takes the table's default TTL and an existing row keeps its expiry, unless isTtlUseTableDefault is set. GetRow reports timeOfExpiration. Expired rows are hidden at once and deleted by a sweep every ttl-sweep-interval-seconds.
  • A row written before an ALTER TABLE reads back in the current schema: a dropped column is gone and an added one shows its default.

docs.title: SQL subset
docs.text:
[DECLARE $var TYPE; ...]
SELECT * | expr [AS name], ... FROM table [[AS] alias]
  [WHERE condition]
  [ORDER BY expr [ASC|DESC] [NULLS FIRST|LAST], ...]
  [LIMIT n] [OFFSET n]
  • Conditions: =, !=, <>, <, <=, >, >=, AND, OR, NOT, IS [NOT] NULL, EXISTS, [NOT] IN (...), [NOT] BETWEEN a AND b.
  • Expressions: string, number and boolean literals, NULL, $variables, dotted JSON paths ($u.info.address.city, u.info.city or info.city), + - * /, and the aggregates count(*), count, min, max, sum and avg.
  • Variables come from QueryDetails variables, keyed with or without $. A declared variable with no value is 400.
  • isPrepared: true takes the statement PrepareStatement returned.
  • Without ORDER BY, rows come back in primary key order.
  • Not supported, 400 InvalidParameter: UPDATE, INSERT, UPSERT and DELETE statements, GROUP BY, functions other than the five aggregates, and mixing aggregates with plain expressions.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
E="--endpoint http://localhost:4599"
TENANCY=ocid1.tenancy.oc1..flocilocaltenancy0000000000000000000000000000000000000000

oci nosql table create $E --compartment-id "$TENANCY" --name users \
  --ddl-statement "CREATE TABLE users (id INTEGER, name STRING, info JSON, PRIMARY KEY (id))" \
  --wait-for-state SUCCEEDED
oci nosql row update $E --table-name-or-id users --compartment-id "$TENANCY" \
  --value '{"id": 1, "name": "ana", "info": {"city": "Lima"}}' --force
oci nosql row get $E --table-name-or-id users --compartment-id "$TENANCY" --key id:1
oci nosql query execute $E --compartment-id "$TENANCY" \
  --statement "SELECT name FROM users u WHERE u.info.city = 'Lima'"

docs.title: Inferred behavior
docs.text:
These points are not stated by the OCI SDK models, the CLI or the Terraform provider under local/oracle, nor by the snapshotted Oracle documentation. They are floci-oci's best reading and may differ from the real service:

  • GetRow of a missing row is a 200 with no value and no etag.
  • The table OCID type is ocid1.nosqltable.
  • A table created without tableLimits is ON_DEMAND with 25 GB of storage and zero read and write units (the SDK model states that ON_DEMAND tables report zero units).
  • A CREATE TABLE for a name that already exists is 409 NotAuthorizedOrResourceAlreadyExists, or, with IF NOT EXISTS, a succeeded work request naming the existing table. A duplicate index name is the same 409.
  • ddlStatement after an ALTER TABLE is the ALTER statement, not a regenerated CREATE.
  • An ALTER TABLE that drops a column removes that column's values from every row, without changing the row versions. A column added later under the same name reads as its DEFAULT (or null) in the existing rows.
  • Column type is the upper-case DDL spelling (INTEGER, TIMESTAMP(3), ARRAY(STRING)); a UUID column is STRING with isAsUuid. Oracle's reference writes type names in upper case, but no source shows the REST field.
  • An ENUM value must match one of the declared symbols exactly, case included. A RECORD value names its fields case-insensitively, may not name a field the type does not declare, and is stored with every declared field, an absent one as null.
  • schema.ttl for an hour-based TTL is rounded up to whole days.
  • Row versions are opaque base64 counters, and the row etag equals the version.
  • usage units are nominal: one read or write unit per row operation, and one read unit per row scanned by a query.
  • ListTables sorts by timeCreated descending by default; ListIndexes by name ascending.
  • A row TTL is counted from the write, without rounding to an hour or day boundary.
  • Query semantics follow the Oracle NoSQL SQL reference, which is not in the local corpus: comparisons with SQL NULL or a missing field are unknown, so the row is filtered out; values of different types are never equal; ORDER BY sorts numbers before strings before booleans, with nulls last ascending and first descending; an unnamed SELECT expression is named after its last path step, or Column_<n>.
  • Query arithmetic is exact. Integer operands give INTEGER or LONG, and a sum, difference, product or negation outside the LONG range widens to NUMBER instead of wrapping; SUM over integers does the same. A FLOAT or DOUBLE operand gives a DOUBLE, and a NUMBER operand with integer or NUMBER operands gives a NUMBER. Division always gives a DOUBLE.
  • DeleteWorkRequest on a finished work request is 409 Conflict. Every emulated work request is finished, so a cancel always reports that.
  • A PrepareStatement result is the statement text, base64-encoded; queryPlan is not returned.
  • A table name in a query that does not exist is 404 NotAuthorizedOrNotFound.

docs.title: Notes & limitations
docs.text:
• No throughput or storage limits are enforced, and ListTableUsage returns no records.
  • Indexes are recorded for read-back only: queries scan the table, and ORDER BY works on any expression, not only on an indexed or primary key prefix as on the real service.
  • Child tables (parent.child), replicas and multi-region tables, frozen schemas, auto-reclaimable expiry and the service configuration with KMS keys are not implemented.

docs.title: Notifications
docs.text: OCI Notifications (ONS), API version 20181201. Topics fan published messages out to their subscriptions: HTTPS endpoints get a real POST, function subscriptions invoke the function, and email, Slack, PagerDuty and SMS messages are recorded in an inspection endpoint instead of being sent. Events rules with an ONS action publish to a topic. Served on port 4599 beside the Functions and Events APIs, which share the same version prefix.

docs.title: Supported operations
docs.text: Area Operations Topics CreateTopic, GetTopic, ListTopics, UpdateTopic, DeleteTopic, ChangeTopicCompartment Subscriptions CreateSubscription, GetSubscription, ListSubscriptions, UpdateSubscription, DeleteSubscription, ChangeSubscriptionCompartment, GetConfirmSubscription, GetUnsubscription, ResendSubscriptionConfirmation Messages PublishMessage

docs.title: Wire notes
docs.text:
• Every operation is synchronous. Create, get and update return the resource with an etag and honour if-match; delete returns 204, and the deleted resource then answers 404 NotAuthorizedOrNotFound. ListTopics and ListSubscriptions return bare arrays with opc-next-page. ListTopics sorts by TIMECREATED (the default, newest first) or LIFECYCLESTATE.
  • A topic is ACTIVE at once and carries a six-character shortTopicId. Its name must be unique (409 Conflict). apiEndpoint is the emulator's base URL. Deleting a topic also deletes its subscriptions.
  • A subscription must be created in its topic's compartment (400 InvalidParameter otherwise), and an unknown topicId is 400 RelatedResourceNotAuthorizedOrNotFound. protocol is one of CUSTOM_HTTPS, EMAIL, HTTPS, ORACLE_FUNCTIONS, PAGERDUTY, SLACK and SMS.
  • Endpoints are checked per protocol: URL protocols need an http or https URL without query parameters, EMAIL an address, SMS an E.164 number, and ORACLE_FUNCTIONS an existing function while Functions is enabled. A URL that names the instance metadata address is refused.
  • GetSubscription returns the delivery policy as a JSON string in deliverPolicy, and ListSubscriptions returns it as an object in deliveryPolicy, as the SDK models do. The default is {"backoffRetryPolicy":{"maxRetryDuration":7200000,"policyType":"EXPONENTIAL"}}. UpdateSubscription answers with UpdateSubscriptionDetails (deliveryPolicy, tags), not the subscription.
  • GetUnsubscription answers with a bare JSON string.
  • PublishMessage takes body (required, at most 64 KB) and title, and returns messageId and timeStamp. With the messageType: JSON header, body must be a JSON object with a default key. Email subscriptions receive its Email value when present, and every other subscription receives default.
  • Subscription OCIDs use onssubscription and topic OCIDs onstopic.

docs.title: Confirmation
docs.text:
A function subscription is ACTIVE at once. Every other subscription is PENDING and receives a confirmation message carrying a confirmation URL. Opening that URL (an unsigned GET .../subscriptions/{id}/confirmation?token=...&protocol=...) makes it ACTIVE. Messages go only to ACTIVE subscriptions.

  • HTTPS endpoints receive the confirmation as a POST with Content-Type: application/json, a {"ConfirmationURL": "..."} body, and the X-OCI-NS-MessageType: SubscriptionConfirmation, X-OCI-NS-ConfirmationURL and X-OCI-NS-SubscriptionId headers.
  • For email, Slack, PagerDuty and SMS, read the confirmation URL from the inspection endpoint below.

The confirmation response carries an unsubscribeUrl. Opening it deletes the subscription.

docs.title: Delivery
docs.text:
Protocol Delivery CUSTOM_HTTPS, HTTPS A POST to the endpoint, with Basic authentication taken from credentials in the URL ORACLE_FUNCTIONS The function is invoked with the message as its body (a synthetic result in Functions mock mode); skipped while Functions is disabled EMAIL, SLACK, PAGERDUTY, SMS Recorded only; nothing leaves the emulator

HTTPS deliveries carry Content-Type, X-OCI-NS-MessageId, X-OCI-NS-TopicOcid, X-OCI-NS-TopicName, X-OCI-NS-MessageType and X-OCI-NS-UnsubscribeURL. A published message is sent as text/plain; charset=UTF-8, and an Events envelope as application/json. Connect and read timeouts are both 5 seconds.

A delivery that fails (an error, a timeout, or a status outside 2xx) is retried at once, then after 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 and 32 minutes, repeating every 32 minutes, until the subscription's maxRetryDuration runs out. The message is then discarded.

docs.title: Inspection endpoint
docs.text:
GET /_floci-oci/notifications/messages (also under /_floci) lists every message sent to a subscription endpoint, oldest first, and keeps the last 1000. It filters on topicId, subscriptionId and protocol. DELETE clears the list. This is a floci-oci endpoint, not an OCI API.

{
  "messages": [
    {
      "messageId": "...", "messageType": "SubscriptionConfirmation",
      "topicId": "ocid1.onstopic...", "topicName": "alerts",
      "subscriptionId": "ocid1.onssubscription...", "protocol": "EMAIL",
      "endpoint": "ops@example.com", "title": null, "body": "{\"ConfirmationURL\":\"...\"}",
      "contentType": "application/json", "confirmationUrl": "http://localhost:4599/20181201/...",
      "unsubscribeUrl": "...", "timestamp": "2026-11-19T10:00:00Z",
      "status": "CAPTURED", "attempts": 1, "lastError": null
    }
  ]
}

status is CAPTURED for recorded protocols, and DELIVERED, RETRYING, FAILED or SKIPPED for the others.

docs.title: Events integration
docs.text: An Events rule action with actionType: ONS publishes the matching event's CloudEvents envelope to topicId. An unknown topic is 400 RelatedResourceNotAuthorizedOrNotFound while Notifications is enabled. While it is disabled, ONS actions are stored but not delivered.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
E="--endpoint http://localhost:4599"
TENANCY=ocid1.tenancy.oc1..flocilocaltenancy0000000000000000000000000000000000000000

TOPIC=$(oci ons topic create $E --compartment-id "$TENANCY" --name alerts --query data.\"topic-id\" --raw-output)
oci ons subscription create $E --compartment-id "$TENANCY" --topic-id "$TOPIC" \
  --protocol EMAIL --subscription-endpoint ops@example.com
curl -s http://localhost:4599/_floci-oci/notifications/messages   # open the confirmationUrl
oci ons message publish $E --topic-id "$TOPIC" --body "disk full" --title Alert

docs.title: Notes and limitations
docs.text:
These are floci-oci's choices where Oracle's documentation is silent:

  • X-OCI-NS-MessageType is Notification on published messages.
  • The confirmation and unsubscribe URLs point at GetConfirmSubscription and GetUnsubscription.
  • The confirmation message text.
  • Topic names are unique within a tenancy and region.

Messages are not signed (no X-OCI-NS-Signature headers), confirmation URLs do not expire, the per-topic publish rate limit is not enforced, and Notifications emits no Events of its own.

docs.title: Object Storage
docs.text: OCI Object Storage — unversioned paths under /n/{namespace}/b/{bucket}/o/{object}.

docs.title: Supported operations
docs.text: Area Operations Namespace GetNamespace (/n), GetNamespaceMetadata Buckets Create, Get, Head, List, Update (including versioning), Delete (must hold no objects or object versions) Objects Put (Content-MD5 check, opc-meta-*, conditional headers), Get (Range → 206), Head, Delete; versionId on Get, Head and Delete Listing ListObjects with prefix/start/end/delimiter/limit/fields, nextStartWith truncation; ListObjectVersions (/objectversions), paged with opc-next-page Actions RenameObject; CopyObject (sourceVersionId, async, work request, terminal status COMPLETED); BatchDeleteObjects (per-object success/failure results, optional per-entry ifMatch, isSkipDeletedResult) Multipart CreateMultipartUpload, UploadPart, Commit, Abort, List Pre-authenticated requests Create, Get, List, Delete; anonymous data path via /p/{token}/… Lifecycle policies PutObjectLifecyclePolicy, GetObjectLifecyclePolicy, DeleteObjectLifecyclePolicy (/l); see below Replication CreateReplicationPolicy, GetReplicationPolicy, ListReplicationPolicies, DeleteReplicationPolicy, ListReplicationSources, MakeBucketWritable Work requests Get, List, errors, logs (unversioned at /workRequests) Amazon S3 Compatibility API See below

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
TENANCY=ocid1.tenancy.oc1..flocilocaltenancy0000000000000000000000000000000000000000
E="--endpoint http://localhost:4599"

oci os ns get $E
oci os bucket create $E --compartment-id "$TENANCY" --namespace floci-local --name demo
echo "hello" > /tmp/hello.txt
oci os object put $E --namespace floci-local --bucket-name demo \
  --file /tmp/hello.txt --name hello.txt
oci os object get $E --namespace floci-local --bucket-name demo \
  --name hello.txt --file -

docs.title: Notes & limitations
docs.text:
• Each tenancy has its own namespace, the same in every region, as on real OCI. The default tenancy (unsigned requests, or default-tenancy-id) uses floci-oci.default-namespace (default floci-local); any other signing tenancy gets a stable 12 character namespace derived from its OCID. GetNamespace returns the caller's, and with ?compartmentId=<tenancy OCID> that tenancy's (a compartment OCID resolves to the caller's namespace).
  • A namespace in the path that is not the caller's is answered with 404 NamespaceNotFound, as on real OCI. Ask GetNamespace for the namespace instead of hard-coding one.
  • CreatePreauthenticatedRequest returns accessUri, the relative /p/{token}/n/… path, and fullPath, the absolute URL: the request's host when it names a region, otherwise FLOCI_OCI_BASE_URL (or FLOCI_OCI_HOSTNAME). As on real OCI, the URL is shown only at creation: Get and List return the summary, with neither field.
  • Pre-authenticated request URLs work for every tenancy: the token is looked up across tenancies in the request's region, must match the namespace in the URL, and acts as the tenancy that created it.
  • CopyObject honours destinationRegion (required, as on real OCI): the destination bucket must exist in that region and the copy lands there. The copy completes immediately; its work request (COMPLETED) is read from the source region.
  • Content-MD5 is verified on upload; opc-content-md5 is returned.
  • Buckets emit createbucket, updatebucket and deletebucket events, and objects emit createobject, updateobject and deleteobject on buckets created or updated with objectEventsEnabled: true. Rules in Events deliver them to Functions and Streaming.
  • CommitMultipartUpload returns opc-multipart-md5: the Base64 MD5 of the committed parts' binary MD5 digests in part-number order, followed by - and the part count. GetObject and HeadObject return the same value for multipart objects, in place of content-md5.
  • Deleting a bucket that still holds objects, previous versions or delete markers answers 409 BucketNotEmpty.
  • Retention rules are not implemented yet.

docs.title: Versioning
docs.text:
A bucket's versioning is Disabled by default. Create a bucket with "versioning": "Enabled", or update it to Enabled or Suspended. As on real OCI:

  • Versioning can be suspended but never disabled again: "versioning": "Disabled" on an update is 400 InvalidParameter.
  • Every object has a version ID, on unversioned buckets too. PutObject, GetObject, HeadObject, CommitMultipartUpload and RenameObject return it in the version-id header.
  • On an Enabled bucket an upload keeps the object it replaces as a previous version, and a delete without versionId keeps the object and adds a delete marker. That DeleteObject answers version-id (the marker's) and is-delete-marker: true.
  • A delete with versionId removes that version, object or delete marker, for good, and answers last-modified only. Deleting the delete marker brings the object back.
  • A Suspended bucket uploads and deletes like a Disabled one and keeps its earlier versions.
  • GetObject with versionId reads a previous version. CopyObject with sourceVersionId copies one, and the copy becomes the latest version at the destination.
  • ListObjectVersions returns {"items": [...], "prefixes": [...]}, by name and then newest first. Every item has name, timeModified, versionId and isDeleteMarker; fields adds size, etag, md5, timeCreated and storageTier to object versions.
  • Only the latest version is replicated, and a replication destination cannot be versioned.

floci-oci's own choices, where no OCI source states the behaviour:

  • When the latest version is deleted by versionId, or deleted on a Suspended bucket, the newest previous version becomes the latest unless it is a delete marker.
  • GetObject and HeadObject on a delete marker's versionId answer 404 ObjectNotFound, and a delete without versionId on an object whose latest version is a marker does too.
  • RenameObject deletes the source the way DeleteObject does, so on an Enabled bucket the source keeps its versions and gets a delete marker.
  • Enabling versioning on a replication destination answers 409 Conflict, and creating a policy towards a versioned bucket answers 409 ReplicationPolicyConflict.
  • opc-next-page names the last entry of the page, not an offset, so deleting a page of versions before asking for the next one skips nothing.

docs.title: Lifecycle policies
docs.text:
A bucket has at most one object lifecycle policy, replaced as a whole by every PUT /n/{namespace}/b/{bucket}/l, as on real OCI.

  • Put and Get answer {timeCreated, items} with an etag. Put honours if-match and if-none-match: *; Delete honours if-match and answers 204. A policy with no rules (items: [] or no items) is accepted, which is what the Terraform provider sends first.
  • A bucket with no policy answers 404 LifecyclePolicyNotFound on Get and Delete.
  • Rules need name, action (ARCHIVE, INFREQUENT_ACCESS, DELETE, ABORT), timeAmount, timeUnit (DAYS or YEARS) and isEnabled. target is objects, previous-object-versions or multipart-uploads; ABORT goes with multipart-uploads and only there. Every field reads back as it was sent, and a missing target stays missing.
  • Limits from Oracle's lifecycle page: 1,000 rules a policy, 20 patterns a name filter, patterns of 1 to 1,024 characters. Patterns use *, ?, \ and [...] (a set, or one a-z range); a group cannot start with ^ or :. Exclusions win over inclusions, and a name matching either an inclusion pattern or an inclusion prefix is included.
  • timeAmount cannot be negative. Oracle documents no minimum, so 0 is accepted and means "at the next midnight UTC".
  • An object's age counts from its last modification, rounded up to midnight UTC; a year is 365.2425 days. A previous version's age counts from when it stopped being the latest version, even if the version that replaced it is deleted later, and an upload's from when it was created.
  • What a rule does when it is due:
  • DELETE on objects deletes the latest version as DeleteObject does, so a bucket with versioning Enabled keeps it as a previous version under a delete marker. A rule with no target acts on objects.
  • DELETE on previous-object-versions deletes those versions for good. Delete markers are left.
  • ABORT drops uncommitted multipart uploads and their parts.
  • ARCHIVE and INFREQUENT_ACCESS are stored and validated but change nothing: storage tiers and archival are not emulated.
  • Rules run every FLOCI_OCI_SERVICES_OBJECTSTORAGE_LIFECYCLE_SWEEP_INTERVAL_SECONDS (60 by default), not once a day as on real OCI, so a due object goes soon after it becomes due. Destinations of a replication policy are read-only and are skipped.

docs.title: Replication
docs.text:
A replication policy on a source bucket copies its writes into a destination bucket, in another region or the same one. As on real OCI:

  • A source has at most one policy (a second one is 409 ReplicationPolicyConflict), a destination has at most one source, and a destination cannot also be a source.
  • The destination bucket must exist first; policy creation does not create it.
  • Only changes made after the policy exists are replicated: puts, multipart commits, renames, copies into the source, deletes and batch deletes. A replica keeps the source's name, data, metadata, ETag and MD5.
  • The source reads replicationEnabled: true and cannot be deleted while it has a policy (403 BucketReplicationEnabled). The destination reads isReadOnly: true.
  • The policy id is a UUID, and timeLastSync is null until the first change is replicated.
  • MakeBucketWritable on the destination stops replication: the bucket becomes writable, and the source's policy moves to CLIENT_ERROR until it is deleted.
  • Deleting the policy makes both buckets ordinary again.

floci-oci's own choices, where no OCI source states the behaviour:

  • Replication is synchronous: a change reaches the destination before the source request answers. Real OCI replicates asynchronously with an unstated lag; a zero lag is one valid case of it.
  • A write or delete on a read-only destination (including through a pre-authenticated request), and deleting a read-only destination bucket, answer 409 Conflict.
  • A destination that already has a source, or is itself a source, answers 409 ReplicationPolicyConflict.
  • MakeBucketWritable on a bucket that is not a destination answers 409 Conflict.

docs.title: Amazon S3 Compatibility API
docs.text:
S3 clients reach the same buckets and objects on OCI's S3 host, <namespace>.compat.objectstorage.<region>.<domain>, path style (/<bucket>/<object>). Locally that is http://<namespace>.compat.objectstorage.<region>.localhost.floci.io:4599, which resolves to 127.0.0.1. A request is recognised by that Host alone; every other request reaches the native API as before.

Area Operations Service ListBuckets (GetService) Buckets PutBucket, HeadBucket, DeleteBucket, GetBucketLocation, GetBucketVersioning (Status from the bucket's versioning), Get/Put/DeleteBucketTagging (the bucket's freeform tags) Objects PutObject, GetObject (Range), HeadObject, DeleteObject, DeleteObjects, CopyObject (x-amz-copy-source, x-amz-metadata-directive); versionId on GetObject, HeadObject, DeleteObject and the copy source Listing ListObjects (v1, marker) and ListObjectsV2 (continuation-token, start-after), with prefix, delimiter, max-keys Multipart CreateMultipartUpload, UploadPart, CompleteMultipartUpload, AbortMultipartUpload, ListParts, ListMultipartUploads
  • Requests are signed with SigV4 and a Customer Secret Key (Identity /20160918/users/{userId}/customerSecretKeys). The access key decides the tenancy and user; an access key no key owns reaches the default tenancy. Signatures are never checked.
  • Buckets created over S3 land in the namespace's defaultS3CompartmentId (the root compartment), as on real OCI.
  • ETags are the hex MD5 S3 clients expect; a multipart object's is the hex MD5 of the part MD5s followed by -<parts>. x-amz-meta-* maps to opc-meta-*.
  • aws-chunked uploads (STREAMING-* payloads, with or without trailing checksums) are decoded; chunk signatures and trailing checksums are not checked.
  • Errors are S3 XML (NoSuchBucket, NoSuchKey, BucketNotEmpty, NoSuchUpload, ...).
  • PutObject honours If-None-Match: * and If-Match, compared with the hex MD5 ETag (412 PreconditionFailed). CompleteMultipartUpload needs every part's ETag and the parts in ascending order (InvalidPart, InvalidPartOrder).
  • GetObject and HeadObject honour If-Match (412 PreconditionFailed) and If-None-Match (304 Not Modified). CopyObject honours x-amz-copy-source-if-match and x-amz-copy-source-if-none-match against the source's ETag.
  • ListObjects and ListObjectsV2 honour encoding-type=url. In ListObjectsV2 with a delimiter, a start-after inside a folder skips that folder's common prefix.
  • A bucket subresource floci-oci does not serve (?policy, ?acl, ?cors, ...) answers 501 NotImplemented; it never runs the plain bucket operation.
  • SigV4 credentials only count on the S3 host. Deleting an Identity user deletes its Customer Secret Keys, and turning Object Storage off turns this API off too: an S3 host then answers 503 and never reaches a native route. Customer Secret Key writes are accepted only in the home region.
  • Version IDs are the native ones. PutObject, GetObject, HeadObject, CopyObject and CompleteMultipartUpload return x-amz-version-id; CopyObject also returns x-amz-copy-source-version-id. A DeleteObject that leaves a delete marker returns x-amz-delete-marker: true and the marker's version ID. versionId=null names the current version, since every Object Storage object has a real version ID. An unknown version ID answers 404 NoSuchKey. Versioning is turned on or suspended through the native API: Oracle's supported list names neither PutBucketVersioning nor ListObjectVersions, so floci-oci does not serve them.
  • Oracle's supported list does not name CopyObject or ListObjectsV2; floci-oci serves them because boto3, the AWS CLI and rclone use them. SSE-C and KMS headers, ACLs, policies and the virtual-host vhcompat endpoint are not implemented.
import boto3
from botocore.config import Config

s3 = boto3.client("s3", region_name="us-ashburn-1",
                  endpoint_url="http://floci-local.compat.objectstorage.us-ashburn-1.localhost.floci.io:4599",
                  aws_access_key_id="<customer secret key id>", aws_secret_access_key="<key>",
                  config=Config(s3={"addressing_style": "path"}))
s3.put_object(Bucket="demo", Key="hello.txt", Body=b"hello")

docs.title: Organizations
docs.text: OCI Organizations (the Tenant Manager control plane), API version 20230401. A parent tenancy creates child tenancies; together they form an organization, and each child is linked to the parent per feature. Real OCI serves it on organizations.{region}.oci.{domain}; floci-oci serves it on port 4599 with the other services.
